title: Follow-ups from a24bcb7 review: CI flake + plateau-detector hardening
description: Commit a24bcb7 (static-scene false-plateau fix: RTP counters as primary liveness signal in DoorVideoFrameView + door-video.html) was reviewed and judged correct, but the review surfaced three follow-ups: (1) CI on main is RED because of a pre-existing flaky wall-clock test (retryingTestsCompleteFastNoRealSleeping, GateClientTests.swift:615-631) that fails under parallel/CI load — unrelated to the commit but blocking green CI; (2) the new pure decision function DoorVideoFrameView.rtpCountersShowProgress was explicitly factored out for testability but sits in the app target, which has no test target (structural gap tracked as gateopener-4ub.22) — the narrow fix is moving the pure logic into GateOpenerCore where tests exist; (3) a minor liveness-window defect: when a poll cannot obtain RTP counters, pollOnce() resets lastRTPCounters to nil, so the NEXT successful sample of a DEAD stream (cumulative counters nonzero) counts once as 'progress', extending the 2.5s plateau by up to one interval per gap. Design: fix the flake deterministically via the already-injectable RetryPolicy.sleep; move RTPCounters + rtpCountersShowProgress to GateOpenerCore with unit tests; then change the gap-handling to retain the last-known baseline instead of nulling it (safe because a counter DECREASE is already treated as no-progress).

title: Ship a notarized DMG on GitHub Releases with in-app self-update
description:
GOAL
Ship GateOpener as a notarized DMG on GitHub Releases, with in-app self-update: the running app discovers a newer version, verifies it, and replaces itself in place. No Sparkle, no server, no stored credential.

DESIGN IS GIVEN, NOT TO BE INVENTED
The operator supplied a reference write-up extracted from a working implementation (GPGuard, 2026-08-28) with three source files: UpdateManifest.swift (manifest model + tolerant SemanticVersion), UpdateInstaller.swift (verification + self-replacing swap), Makefile.release-excerpt (publish side). FOLLOW IT. The porting checklist is explicit about what is app-specific.
Shape:
1. Every release publishes TWO assets: the DMG plus a small STABLE-NAMED JSON manifest {latestVersion, notes, dmgURL, dmgSHA256}. The digest is computed from the artifact just built, so the manifest can never describe a different binary.
2. Discovery uses https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/latest/download/<stable-asset-name>, which always 302s to the newest release's asset of that name. No API call, no token, no rate limit.
3. Comparison FAILS CLOSED: SemanticVersion accepts 1-4 dot-separated integers, treats missing trailing components as 0 (1.4 == 1.4.0), returns nil for anything else. An unparseable version on EITHER side means "no update available". Never prompt to upgrade to something you cannot order.
4. verify() throws unless BOTH hold: streaming SHA-256 in 1 MiB chunks (never loads the DMG into memory) matches dmgSHA256, AND `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` exits 0. Keep this EXACTLY as-is; the reference says it is the whole security story.
5. The swap: a running .app cannot overwrite itself. Write a /bin/sh script to NSTemporaryDirectory() mode 0755, launch it DETACHED via nohup, pass DMG path + getpid() + install dir + bundle name (every interpolated path through shQuote), then NSApp.terminate. The script spins on `kill -0 $PID`, then hdiutil attach -nobrowse -noverify -plist, parses the mount point, rm -rf the old bundle, cp -R the new one in place, hdiutil detach, open.

WHY cp -R IN PLACE MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY
Same path + same Developer ID identity means TCC grants, login-item registration, and — critically for this app — the KEYCHAIN ACL GRANT survive the upgrade. This project already lost days to keychain re-prompts caused by an unstable ad-hoc signing identity (see gateopener-sal). An updater that broke the grant on every upgrade would reintroduce exactly that pain.

DROP ALL THE GPGuard ENTERPRISE SCAFFOLDING
GPGuard published to GitHub Enterprise, which 401s unauthenticated clients, so it opened URLs in the user's browser, registered a custom UTI, added CFBundleDocumentTypes, used NSOpenPanel for scoped access, and had a "it's been N days" nag that existed only because it could not poll. This repo will be PUBLIC, so the app can just URLSession-GET the manifest. Delete promptForDownloadedDMG and all of the above.

TWO OPERATOR-ONLY PREREQUISITES — the graph is sequenced so each is needed at exactly ONE point
1. A GitHub remote must exist. There is none today (`git remote -v` is empty). The operator creates it; agents MUST NOT run `gh repo create`, create a remote, or push.
2. Notarization credentials. The operator has a Developer ID certificate but `xcrun notarytool history` reports "Must provide credentials". The operator has said they will create a new App Store Connect API key WHEN WE GET THERE and want to be told when, with a reminder of how. That moment is the notarization bead. Agents MUST NOT create, store, or handle that credential.
NOTE THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL: verify() requires `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` to exit 0, which passes only for NOTARIZED artifacts. Developer ID signing alone fails it. Skipping notarization would gut half the security model and leave an updater that installs whatever the network hands it.

SECURITY PRECONDITION
This repo has been driven against the operator's LIVE Comelit account for days. Bead gateopener-4ub.13 already requires auditing the FULL git history (git log -p, not just the working tree) for the operator's password, access/refresh tokens, and .comelit_token.json. That audit must pass before anything is published. It is wired as a dependency here.

title: Stale frame from the previous session shows when the video overlay reopens
description:
GOAL
When the live-video overlay opens a SECOND time, it must never show a frame from the PREVIOUS session. The user reports: "when the pip window shows up a second time, it seems to show the last image from the last run, which is confusing."

WHY IT MATTERS
A stale frame is worse than a blank panel: it silently shows the user the state of their gate from minutes ago as though it were live. Someone could look at an old frame, see nobody at the gate, and act on it. Correctness of what is shown matters more here than smoothness.

USER NARROWED IT (2026-08-28, later message): "I just did it again from the menu, and it didn't happen, so maybe it's only when it shows when opening the gate."
So the STALE FRAME reproduces on the GATE-OPEN path but NOT on the "View Door" menu path. Treat that as the primary lead — but verify rather than assume, since a single negative observation is not proof of absence.

WHY THAT IS CONSISTENT WITH THE TRACED MECHANISM, AND WHAT IT IMPLIES
Both paths swap content on `.streaming`:
  - DoorVideoOverlayController.swift ~:127-128  -> presentFrameView()
  - OverlayWindowController.swift ~:466-468     -> setContent(openVideoFrameView)
So the underlying timing flaw (swapping in a frame view that has no current-session image yet) is SHARED. What differs is what the swap REPLACES, and therefore whether a human notices:
  - "View Door": replaces a plain "Connecting..." placeholder with a frame view that itself shows a "Connecting..." label. One placeholder for a near-identical placeholder — visually a no-op, so nothing looks wrong even though the same premature swap happens.
  - Gate open: replaces the PLAYING canned gate animation. The animation is visibly cut off, and any stale/blank content in the frame view is exposed.
This explains BOTH user reports with ONE cause and predicts exactly the asymmetry observed. It also means a fix targeted only at the open path may leave the same latent flaw in the View Door path — prefer a shared fix, and say so if you cannot.

SECOND SYMPTOM, REPORTED BY THE USER — ALMOST CERTAINLY THE SAME BUG
"I kind of liked the 'slowly opening curtains' effect, that distracts the user from the delay for live video to appear, and I didn't see that either."
So on the gate-open path the canned gate-opening animation is ALSO not being seen. The user explicitly values it: it covers the ~6s wait for live video, which is the whole reason it was kept.

LIKELY SINGLE ROOT CAUSE FOR BOTH SYMPTOMS (traced, not yet proven — the diagnosis bead must confirm)
OverlayWindowController.handleOpenVideoState(_:) at ~:466 swaps content on `.streaming`:
    case .streaming:
        guard let openVideoFrameView, openVideoSession != nil else { return }
        setContent(openVideoFrameView)
But `.streaming` fires as soon as framesDecoded > 0 in the SESSION — the DoorVideoFrameView has not yet completed its own first captureFrameJpeg poll and decode, so it has NO image at that moment. DoorVideoFrameView carries its own "Connecting..." label which it hides only when the first image is assigned (DoorVideoFrameView.swift ~:251-252).
CONSEQUENCE: the canned animation is torn out and replaced by an image-less frame view. The user therefore sees the curtains CUT OFF partway rather than playing through, replaced by a label (or, on a reopen, by whatever stale content that view path yields — the first reported symptom).
So the fix is likely ONE change, not two: do not swap the panel to the live view until a frame FROM THAT SESSION has actually been decoded and is ready to display. Swap on first-frame-ready, not on `.streaming`.

WHAT THE USER WANTS, EXPLICITLY
- The canned gate-opening animation should PLAY, visibly, covering the connect delay. It is not decoration; it is the thing that makes the ~6s wait tolerable.
- Then live video appears.
- Never a frame from a previous session.
Treat "the curtains are visible on the open path" as a first-class done-criterion, not a side effect of fixing the stale frame.

WHERE THE STALE FRAME COULD COME FROM — investigate, do not assume
Preliminary tracing narrowed this but did NOT settle it:
- DoorVideoOverlayController builds a FRESH DoorVideoFrameView per session (DoorVideoOverlayController.swift ~:85), and OverlayWindowController builds a fresh one per open (~:422). So a reused Swift view holding an old NSImage is NOT the obvious cause.
- DoorVideoSession constructs a NEW WKWebView per session (DoorVideoSession.swift:174) and loads the page fresh (:242), so a reused <video> element is ALSO not the obvious cause.
- BUT the page's capture function guards only on dimensions:
      Resources/door-video.html:188-196 — window.captureFrameJpeg returns null only when video.videoWidth/videoHeight are 0.
  A <video> that has finished a session KEEPS its dimensions and FREEZES on its last decoded frame (this is documented in bd memory gateopener-live-video-architecture and was the root of the plateau-detector bug). So ANY path where a page or view outlives a session will hand back a stale frame that passes that guard.
STRONG CANDIDATES to check, in order:
  1. Does the overlay PANEL still hold the previous session's frame view (or its NSImage) when a new session starts? OverlayWindowController.setContent(_:) installs content, and 12h.2 made re-setting the SAME view a deliberate no-op — if the panel is not reset between sessions, the old image can remain visible until the first new frame lands ~6s later.
  2. Is there a window between show() and the first decoded frame where the panel displays the old content rather than the connecting placeholder?
  3. Is any DoorVideoFrameView/imageView actually reused or cached anywhere (e.g. currentFrameView in DoorVideoOverlayController, openVideoFrameView in OverlayWindowController) across sessions?
  4. Does captureFrameJpeg ever get called against a page whose <video> holds a previous session's frozen frame — e.g. if teardown does not blank it?

DESIGN DIRECTION (not binding, but the bar)
Whatever the cause, the fix should make a stale frame STRUCTURALLY impossible rather than papered over with a timing tweak. Preferred shape: the panel shows the connecting placeholder from the moment a session starts until a frame from THAT session is decoded, and any prior image is cleared at session start rather than left to be overwritten.

CONSTRAINTS — all hard-won, none may regress
- The overlay must NEVER take keyboard focus: orderFrontRegardless() only, never makeKeyAndOrderFront, never NSApp.activate. This is the epic's long-standing acceptance gate.
- Do NOT display the <video> element; keep the canvas-capture architecture (see bd memory gateopener-live-video-architecture for why).
- Keep the byte-comparison plateau detector — a stalled <video> freezes rather than blanking, so identical bytes must not count as a new frame.
- Keep streaming detection on framesDecoded > 0.
- The panel's content view must stay wantsLayer = true or nothing renders at all.
- rtc/offer only; never the power/open endpoint.

title: Live video decodes but the <video> element never paints (0x0)
description:
DISCOVERED during gateopener-12h.3 hardware verification. BLOCKS gateopener-12h.5 (View door UI) — a UI built on contentView today would show a black rectangle.

THE PROBLEM
Real RTP arrives and decodes: pc.getStats() reports packetsReceived and framesDecoded climbing (verified: 16 packets / 8 frames on a live run, ICE connected, ontrack fired for both audio and video). But the page's <video> element does NOT paint:
    hasVideoFrame: false, videoWidth: 0, videoHeight: 0
requestVideoFrameCallback never fires in this WKWebView context either. So the media pipeline works and the presentation layer does not.
DoorVideoSession no longer DEPENDS on this — 12h.3 switched streaming detection to framesDecoded > 0, the spec-guaranteed ground truth — so the session state machine is correct. But contentView (the WKWebView) is what 12h.5 installs into the overlay panel, and if the <video> never paints, the user sees a black tile.

WHY THIS IS FAMILIAR AND MUST NOT BE HAND-WAVED
This is the same SHAPE as gateopener-9kk.12: every signal said the feature worked (panel visible, alpha 1, state correct) while the pixels never arrived, and it survived seven beads of review because everything verified the plumbing and nothing verified the image. Do NOT close this bead on stats, state, or reasoning. Close it on SEEING A PICTURE.

INVESTIGATE — establish the cause before fixing
1. Is the track actually attached to the element? Check that the ontrack handler assigns event.streams[0] (or a new MediaStream with the track) to video.srcObject, and that it happens for the VIDEO track, not just audio. Log video.srcObject, its getVideoTracks(), and each track's readyState/muted/enabled.
2. Is the element allowed to play? WebKit autoplay policy is strict. The element should be muted + playsinline + autoplay; verify video.play() is actually called and that its returned promise does not reject (log the rejection if it does). A rejected play() promise is a classic silent cause.
3. Is the WKWebView being rendered at all? A web view that is never added to a window/view hierarchy, or has zero size, may not composite. The spike ran the page in a VISIBLE window; DoorVideoSession may host it offscreen/hidden. Check the web view's frame, whether it is in a hierarchy, and whether isHidden. THIS IS THE PRIME SUSPECT — an offscreen or zero-sized WKWebView is a very plausible reason decoding proceeds while nothing paints.
4. Check the console for errors inside the page (add a message handler or read via the log array already in door-video.html).
5. Compare against the spike harness at scratchpad/webrtc-spike/ — it ran the same page and the user SAW the camera view, so whatever it did differently is the answer. Diff the hosting setup, not the page.

DO
- Fix so the live camera image actually paints in the view DoorVideoSession exposes for embedding.
- Keep streaming detection on framesDecoded > 0. Do NOT revert it to hasVideoFrame/requestVideoFrameCallback.
- If the fix requires the web view to be in a visible hierarchy, coordinate that with how OverlayWindowController.setContent(_:) installs content — the view will be a subview of the panel's layer-backed content view. Note gateopener-9kk.12: the panel's content view MUST stay wantsLayer = true or nothing renders at all.
- Do not weaken any existing guarantee: token never reaches page JS, no renegotiation/watchdog/reconnect, rtc/offer only, NEVER the power/open endpoint.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A SCREENSHOT (or equivalent captured pixels) showing the actual live door-camera image rendered in the view DoorVideoSession exposes. Not stats. Not state. A picture.
- videoWidth/videoHeight report the real dimensions (expected ~320x240) rather than 0.
- swift build; swift test (126 at filing); GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- Report the root cause plainly, so the next person understands why it did not paint.

title: Live video session on every gate open, all three triggers
description:
INPUT: a working "View door" flow. This bead makes live video ALSO appear on every gate open.

THE USER'S REQUIREMENT (verbatim): "if I open the gate however I open it (click the menu item, choose something from it's right-click menu, or use the shortcut) I get a 'session' of live video so I can see the gate opening."
So ALL THREE triggers must produce live video: the global hotkey, the "Open Gate" menu item, and a left-click on the status item.

THE TIMING PROBLEM — SOLVE IT, DO NOT IGNORE IT
An open completes in ~2s. Live video takes ~4-6s to first frame, dominated by the cloud rtc/offer round trip and NOT reducible by changing WebRTC stacks. So the video arrives AFTER the gate has already opened. That is acceptable and expected — the user wants to SEE THE GATE OPENING and the door stays open longer than the API call takes — but the UI must not look broken in the gap.
REQUIRED BEHAVIOR: on .opening, show the overlay immediately with the existing canned gate-open animation (that is what it is for, and it is instant), AND start a DoorVideoSession in parallel. When the first video frame arrives, swap the panel's content to the live feed via setContent(_:). The session then runs to its natural end, at which point the overlay disappears.
Do NOT make the user wait 5 seconds staring at nothing, and do NOT drop the canned animation — it covers exactly the gap that live video cannot.

DO
1. Drive this from GateState, consistent with the existing design: the overlay observes state and has NO per-trigger code. Do NOT add "if triggered from the menu" branches. All three triggers already funnel through openGate() -> .opening -> onStateChange -> handle(_:).
2. Start the video session on .opening; swap content when the first frame arrives; let the overlay disappear at session end rather than at .succeeded/.idle. NOTE this CHANGES the overlay's lifetime for the open path: it now outlives the ~1.45s hold+fade. Handle that explicitly and comment it — the 9kk.5 reentrancy rules (pendingResolveTask, isResolveFadePending, alpha reset) must still hold, and a second open arriving mid-session must not strand a panel or stack sessions.
3. RESPECT THE EXISTING SETTINGS TOGGLE. AppSettings.showOpenConfirmationOverlay currently governs the confirmation overlay. Decide and implement: does that toggle now also govern live-video-on-open, or does live video need its own preference (the previously-anticipated name was autoShowDoorVideoOnOpen)? A SEPARATE preference is likely right — a user may want instant confirmation without a 30s video every time. Implement whichever you choose, add it to Settings following LaunchAtLoginSectionView's pattern, default it ON to satisfy the user's stated requirement, and JUSTIFY the choice in your report.
4. Failure of the video session must NOT break the confirmation. If video fails or never connects, the canned animation plays and the overlay behaves exactly as it does today. Live video is additive.
5. Focus guarantee is unchanged and non-negotiable: the hotkey path fires while the user is typing in another app. orderFrontRegardless only.
6. Verify ALL THREE triggers BY OBSERVATION. The menu path especially — gateopener-9kk.12 shipped broken precisely because it was argued rather than observed.

SESSION LENGTH IS NOW MEASURED, NOT INHERITED (gateopener-12h.4, 2026-08-28)
Three runs to natural expiry under WKWebView: framesDecoded plateaued at 28.30s, 28.87s, 28.69s from first frame. Spread under 1 second — remarkably stable, and it CONFIRMS the ~28-30s figure previously only inherited from ../comelit's Chromium work. The user's "roughly 30 seconds" is real.

WHAT HAPPENS AT EXPIRY — this shapes the implementation:
  - framesDecoded PLATEAUS at ~28.5s. Media stops.
  - packetsReceived keeps ticking for a few more seconds (trailing packets, no new frames).
  - iceConnectionState/connectionState STAY 'connected' for another ~9-10s, only going 'disconnected' at ~t+38s and 'failed' at ~t+48s.
  - CRITICAL: DoorVideoSession NEVER AUTO-DETECTS ANY OF THIS. Its state stays .streaming indefinitely until stop() is called explicitly. Nothing ends the session on its own today.

REQUIRED: implement expiry detection, because the user's decided behavior is that the overlay DISAPPEARS at session end.
  - PRIMARY SIGNAL: a framesDecoded-plateau detector — no new decoded frame for ~2-3s means the session is over. Use this, not ICE state, which lags the actual video stop by 10-20 seconds and would leave a frozen picture on screen for that whole time.
  - BACKSTOP: a hard timeout around ~35s in case stats polling itself misfires. Do NOT make a bare fixed timer the primary trigger, even though the measured length is stable.
  - Do NOT wait for iceConnectionState to reach disconnected/failed before hiding the overlay.
  - Do NOT implement renegotiation or reconnect to extend the session — explicitly out of scope for this epic.

DONE-CRITERIA
- All three triggers produce: instant canned animation, then live video, then the overlay disappears at session end. Each verified by observation and reported separately.
- Video failure degrades to today's behavior with no stranded panel.
- Rapid repeated opens do not stack sessions or panels.
- Typing in another app is unaffected throughout.
- swift build; swift test; SELFTEST PASS.

title: View door menu item: live camera without opening the gate
description:
INPUT: DoorVideoSession, the fixed setContent (bead .2), and the existing OverlayWindowController.

OUTPUT: a "View door" menu item that shows live camera video in the HUD panel, WITHOUT opening the gate.

DO
1. Add a "View door" item to the status-item menu in StatusItemController.showMenu(), placed above "Open Gate" (seeing who is there logically precedes deciding to open). Follow the existing NSMenuItem construction exactly.
2. On selection: start a DoorVideoSession and present it in the overlay panel.
3. THE PANEL MUST BE INTERACTIVE for this use. OverlayWindowController's init already takes ignoresMouseEvents (default true) precisely for this — construct/configure so the View-door panel accepts clicks and can be dismissed by the user. The gate-open confirmation overlay MUST remain ignoresMouseEvents = true.
4. CONNECTING STATE IS REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL. Measured time-to-first-frame is ~4-6s, dominated by the cloud round trip. A blank panel for 5 seconds reads as broken. Show a clear connecting indication, then swap to video when frames arrive. Use setContent(_:) — bead .2 makes swapping into a visible panel start the incoming content correctly.
5. At session end the overlay DISAPPEARS (user's explicit decision). No frozen last frame, no error, no reconnect.
6. On failure, show a brief human-readable message and then disappear; do not strand the panel.
7. PRESERVE THE FOCUS GUARANTEE for the gate-open path: orderFrontRegardless only, never makeKeyAndOrderFront/NSApp.activate. NOTE the tension and resolve it explicitly: an interactive panel may legitimately need to accept clicks, but must still not steal keyboard focus from the app the user is typing in. If you cannot satisfy both, STOP AND REPORT rather than weakening the focus guarantee.
8. Menu-item triggering runs inside NSMenu's modal tracking loop. Verify the session actually starts from the menu — a prior bug (gateopener-9kk.12) shipped precisely because the menu path was never observed. Observe it, do not argue it.

RENDERING APPROACH IS SETTLED — DO NOT DISPLAY THE <video> ELEMENT (resolved in gateopener-12h.8, 2026-08-28)
A WKWebView only begins compositing once its host window becomes KEY at least once. OverlayWindowController's panel is .nonactivatingPanel and can NEVER become key, so a <video> element inside it stays permanently blank. That is not fixable without giving the panel focus, which is forbidden.
SOLUTION, VERIFIED AGAINST REAL HARDWARE: draw the frame to a HIDDEN CANVAS inside the page and read it out — `window.captureFrameJpeg(quality)` is already in Resources/door-video.html (ported from ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html, where it powered the Python app's MJPEG). This WORKS in a fully non-activating panel: a 320x240 frame was captured and visually confirmed (driveway, cobblestones, railings) with framesDecoded=14, from a panel shown only via orderFrontRegardless().
So: keep the WKWebView OFF-SCREEN/hidden as a pure media engine, and render the captured frames into a plain layer-backed NSView / NSImageView / CALayer.contents that the panel hosts. The web view is never the thing the user looks at.

PRODUCTION RENDERING NOTES
- Poll captureFrameJpeg via callAsyncJavaScript (NEVER evaluateJavaScript — WKErrorDomain code 5 on Promise-returning expressions) at roughly 8-10fps; the reference used a 125ms interval.
- PROFILE THESE, they are untested: JPEG encode + base64 + decode cost per frame, callAsyncJavaScript per-call dispatch overhead, and frame-pacing jitter under sustained polling. The 12h.8 experiment captured a SINGLE frame, not a sustained stream. If sustained polling proves too costly, report it rather than shipping something that pins a CPU.
- Keep DoorVideoSession's streaming detection on framesDecoded > 0 from getStats(). Do NOT switch it to hasVideoFrame.
- The panel content view must stay wantsLayer = true (gateopener-9kk.12) or nothing renders at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FOCUS/CLOSEABILITY TRADEOFF BELOW: it is very likely MOOT. Rendering no longer needs key status, so the panel can stay non-activating AND accept mouse clicks via ignoresMouseEvents = false. Verify empirically anyway — type into another app with the panel visible and confirm no keystroke is lost.

USER RULING ON THE FOCUS/CLOSEABILITY TRADEOFF (2026-08-28) — BINDING
The user was asked to arbitrate in advance and ruled: "If we have to choose between being able to close the video window, and having it steal keyboard focus, I'll choose not having it steal keyboard focus."
So FOCUS WINS. If the two genuinely conflict, ship an overlay that is awkward to dismiss rather than one that grabs keystrokes. Never weaken the focus guarantee to gain a close button.

BUT DO NOT ACCEPT THAT TRADEOFF WITHOUT TESTING — it is very probably FALSE.
An NSPanel can receive MOUSE events without ever becoming KEY. These are independent mechanisms:
  - Keyboard focus is governed by canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain (OverlayPanel already returns false for both) and by using orderFrontRegardless() rather than makeKeyAndOrderFront/NSApp.activate.
  - Mouse delivery is governed by ignoresMouseEvents, already exposed as a SEPARATE constructor parameter on OverlayWindowController precisely for this feature.
Set ignoresMouseEvents = false for the View-door panel and it should accept clicks while still never taking keyboard focus. TRY THIS FIRST and VERIFY EMPIRICALLY: with the panel visible, type into another app (TextEdit or a terminal) and confirm every keystroke lands there and the frontmost app keeps its active title bar. Report that observation explicitly.
Only if click-to-dismiss provably cannot work without focus theft does the user's ruling bite — and then you drop closeability, not the guarantee, and report the finding.

DISMISSAL ROUTES THAT NEED NO KEYBOARD FOCUS AT ALL (prefer these; several can coexist)
  - The session simply ENDING (~28-30s). The user has already decided the overlay DISAPPEARS at session end — that alone means no panel is ever permanently stuck.
  - Click anywhere on the panel, or a small close affordance, with ignoresMouseEvents = false.
  - A menu item toggle (the menu is already the trigger).
  - hide() is safe to call externally as of gateopener-9kk.9 — it cancels pending resolve work and clears state — so an external dismiss will not strand the panel.
Do NOT add a keyboard shortcut that requires the panel to be key. That is the one route that would force focus theft.

SESSION LENGTH IS NOW MEASURED, NOT INHERITED (gateopener-12h.4, 2026-08-28)
Three runs to natural expiry under WKWebView: framesDecoded plateaued at 28.30s, 28.87s, 28.69s from first frame. Spread under 1 second — remarkably stable, and it CONFIRMS the ~28-30s figure previously only inherited from ../comelit's Chromium work. The user's "roughly 30 seconds" is real.

  - packetsReceived keeps ticking for a few more seconds (trailing packets, no new frames).
  - iceConnectionState/connectionState STAY 'connected' for another ~9-10s, only going 'disconnected' at ~t+38s and 'failed' at ~t+48s.
  - CRITICAL: DoorVideoSession NEVER AUTO-DETECTS ANY OF THIS. Its state stays .streaming indefinitely until stop() is called explicitly. Nothing ends the session on its own today.

  - PRIMARY SIGNAL: a framesDecoded-plateau detector — no new decoded frame for ~2-3s means the session is over. Use this, not ICE state, which lags the actual video stop by 10-20 seconds and would leave a frozen picture on screen for that whole time.
  - BACKSTOP: a hard timeout around ~35s in case stats polling itself misfires. Do NOT make a bare fixed timer the primary trigger, even though the measured length is stable.
  - Do NOT wait for iceConnectionState to reach disconnected/failed before hiding the overlay.
  - Do NOT implement renegotiation or reconnect to extend the session — explicitly out of scope for this epic.

DONE-CRITERIA
- "View door" shows live video from the real door, verified BY OBSERVATION (screenshot or equivalent), not by reasoning.
- It does NOT open the gate. Confirm no power/open call is made.
- A connecting state is visible during the ~4-6s wait.
- Overlay disappears at session end.
- Typing in another app is unaffected while the panel is visible.

title: Measure the real door session length under WKWebView
description:
INPUT: a working DoorVideoSession. This bead answers a question the spike explicitly did NOT answer, and the answer drives the UI.

WHY THIS EXISTS
The user's requirement is a "session" of live video, stated as "roughly 30 seconds". ../comelit documented the door stopping RTP at ~28-30s per rtc/offer session — but that was measured against CHROMIUM. The gateopener-yjn spike NEVER observed it under WKWebView: every run was ended by the harness well under 30s (longest ~10-12s). So the 30s figure is INHERITED, NOT PROVEN for WebKit. Building UI timing on an unmeasured number is exactly the kind of assumption that has already bitten this project once.

DO
1. Run ONE DoorVideoSession against real hardware to NATURAL EXPIRY. Do not stop it early.
2. Poll getStats() at a steady interval (~500ms) and record framesDecoded/packetsReceived over time. Log wall-clock from first frame.
3. Determine and REPORT: at what elapsed time does RTP actually stop arriving (framesDecoded plateaus)? Does ICE/DTLS stay connected while media stops, as ../comelit describes, or does the connection drop outright?
4. Repeat 2-3 times to see whether the figure is stable.
5. Record the measured value with `bd remember` in this repo. If it differs materially from ~28-30s, say so loudly — downstream UI depends on it.

DO NOT
- Do not implement renegotiation or reconnect to extend the session. Measuring only.
- Do not call the power/open endpoint. rtc/offer only.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A measured session length with at least 2 data points, recorded via bd remember.
- An explicit statement of what happens at expiry (media stops vs connection drops).
- A recommendation for what the UI should do at expiry, given the user has already decided the overlay DISAPPEARS at session end.
- No production behavior change in this bead — measurement only, though a temporary harness is fine if removed afterward.
close_reason: Measured: 28.30s / 28.87s / 28.69s to framesDecoded plateau across three WKWebView runs to natural expiry. Confirms the previously-inherited ~28-30s figure. Findings and the plateau-detector recommendation recorded in bd memory gateopener-12h-4-measurement-result-2026-08-28 and folded into 12h.5 and 12h.6. Measurement only — no production diff.

title: DoorVideoSession: one live WebRTC session via WKWebView
description:
INPUT: the proven spike recipe. READ FIRST: `bd memories --json` in THIS repo, key gateopener-yjn-spike-result-wkwebview-webkit-s-own AND gateopener-yjn-spike-addendum-answers-to-a-follow. Then read the throwaway harness at scratchpad/webrtc-spike/Sources/WebRTCSpike/main.swift and its webrtc_page.html, and ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html.

OUTPUT: a production DoorVideoSession type in Sources/GateOpener/ that establishes ONE live door-camera WebRTC session via WKWebView and reports its state. NO UI, NO overlay integration — that is a later bead.

DO
1. Create Sources/GateOpener/DoorVideoSession.swift, @MainActor. It owns a WKWebView (hidden/offscreen is fine) and the bundled page.
2. Bundle the WebRTC page as a resource. Copy ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html into Resources/ as door-video.html, STRIPPING the stale-frame watchdog and renegotiation machinery — this app does ONE session and never renegotiates (see the epic). Wire it into the bundle the SAME way Resources/gate-open.mp4 is wired in scripts/build-app.sh; do not invent a second mechanism.
3. Implement the recipe EXACTLY as proven; do not improvise:
   - recvonly transceivers, AUDIO ADDED BEFORE VIDEO (m-line order is load-bearing)
   - createDataChannel('data') so the offer has 3 m-sections, BUNDLE audio(0)/video(1)/application(2)
   - NON-trickle ICE: wait for iceGatheringState === 'complete', then send the full offer in ONE shot
   - pre-resolve stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com to IPs in Swift and inject window.__ICE_SERVERS__ as stun:<ip>:3478 BEFORE the page negotiates
   - PUT the offer from Swift/URLSession: PUT https://api.comelitgroup.com/servicerest/devicecom/endpoint/<ENDPOINT_ID>/rtc/offer, headers authorization: bearer <token>, content-type: application/json, user-agent: ktor-client, body {"sessionId": <uuid4>, "offer": <SDP>} -> 200 {"answer": <SDP>}. '#' in the endpoint id becomes %23 (NOT full percent-encoding).
   - THE BEARER TOKEN MUST NEVER REACH PAGE JS. Get it via GateOpenerCore's TokenManager in Swift only.
4. Camera endpoint selection: friendlyName containing 'entry' (case-insensitive), else endpoint id suffix VIP#EN#SB100001. Reuse the existing discovery path in GateOpenerCore rather than writing a new one.
5. GOTCHA, will cost an hour if missed: plain evaluateJavaScript(_:) fails with WKErrorDomain code 5 on ANY Promise-returning expression. Use callAsyncJavaScript(_:contentWorld:) with an explicit 'return await ...;' body for anything async.
6. Expose a state enum the UI can drive off: at minimum .idle, .connecting, .streaming, .ended(reason), .failed(message). Report state via a callback/closure, matching how GateController exposes onStateChange — do NOT import SwiftUI/Observation into GateOpenerCore (this type lives in the app layer anyway).
7. Provide the AVSampleBuffer/NSView the video renders into, or expose the WKWebView itself for embedding — your choice, justify it. It must be installable via OverlayWindowController.setContent(_:).
8. Explicit teardown: a stop()/close() that tears down the peer connection and the web view so no session or decoder leaks. Must be idempotent.

DO NOT BUILD: renegotiation, a stale-frame watchdog, session continuation, reconnect, or any UI. One session, then it ends.

EDGE CASES
- No network / rtc-offer non-200: surface .failed with a SHORT human-readable message; never crash, never force-unwrap.
- Token unavailable or needsSetup: surface .failed, do not prompt.
- Unbundled process (swift run / self-test): door-video.html will not be found — degrade silently with a logged notice, exactly as GateOpenVideoView does for gate-open.mp4.

DONE-CRITERIA
- swift build; swift test (126 at filing); SELFTEST PASS.
- Verified against REAL HARDWARE: one session reaches .streaming with packetsReceived > 0. Report the actual stats. rtc/offer only — NEVER call the power/open endpoint.
- Report measured time from start() to first frame.
- No changes to GateOpenerCore beyond reusing existing auth/discovery.

title: Fire overlayWillShow when content is swapped into a visible panel
description:
INPUT: OverlayWindowController.setContent(_:) and the OverlayShowHideResponding protocol, both in Sources/GateOpener/OverlayWindowController.swift (merged, working).

PROBLEM (already analysed, see gateopener-12h.1 which this supersedes/absorbs)
setContent(_:) installs a new view into an ALREADY-VISIBLE panel but never fires overlayWillShow() on it, so the incoming content is never started. For a video view that means it sits on frame zero — a black tile.
This is exactly the ordering the live-camera feature uses: show the panel with a connecting state, then swap in the video view once frames arrive. The symptom would look like a WebRTC failure rather than a lifecycle bug, which is expensive to misdiagnose.

DO
1. In setContent(_:), after installing the view: if the panel exists AND is currently visible, invoke overlayWillShow() on the newly installed content. Guard on the panel's isVisible — when not visible, show() will do it, and firing twice must not happen.
2. When content is REPLACED, invoke overlayDidHide() on the OUTGOING content first, so a swapped-out player pauses rather than decoding off-screen.
3. Preserve every existing guarantee: orderFrontRegardless only (never makeKeyAndOrderFront/NSApp.activate), handle(_:) remains the sole presentation driver, the 9kk.5 reentrancy rules (pendingResolveTask cancellation, isResolveFadePending, alpha reset), the 9kk.7 settings gate and Reduce Motion, and the 9kk.9 single-Task.isCancelled-check ordering in fadeOutThenHide().
4. Do NOT reorder or re-present the panel as a side effect of swapping content.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Swapping content into a visible panel starts the new content; swapping out pauses the outgoing one.
- No behavior change when setContent is called before show().
- swift build; swift test (126 at filing); GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.

title: Menu-triggered open does not show the confirmation overlay
description:
REPORTED BY THE USER after installing the merged epic: "I don't see a way to show the video on the menu, that was a specific requirement."

SYMPTOM
Triggering an open from the status-item MENU ("Open Gate") does not visibly show the confirmation overlay, while the global hotkey and a direct left-click on the status item both do.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, verify before fixing)
StatusItemController.showMenu() presents the menu with NSMenu.popUp(positioning:at:in:) at StatusItemController.swift:174. That call is BLOCKING and MODAL — the codebase already documents this at :60-65 — and it spins the run loop in NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode for the whole time the menu is up.
menuOpenGate() calls handleLeftClick(), which dispatches Task { await controller.openGate() }. The .opening state change therefore fans out to OverlayWindowController.handle(_:) while that modal tracking loop may still be active or just unwinding. The overlay's presentation and, critically, its hold-then-fade timing (a 1200ms hold + 250ms NSAnimationContext fade scheduled via Task) can be starved or mis-sequenced in that mode, so the panel either never appears or appears and is torn down without being seen.
NOTE this is precisely the verification gap flagged and knowingly accepted in bead gateopener-9kk.6: synthetic clicks cannot drive NSMenu's modal tracking loop, so the menu path was closed on a code-identity argument (menuOpenGate simply calls handleLeftClick) rather than on observation. The code-identity argument was correct about the TRIGGER but missed that the RUN-LOOP CONTEXT differs — the menu path runs its state fan-out under modal event tracking, the left-click path does not.

DO
1. REPRODUCE FIRST and confirm the mechanism before changing anything. Add temporary logging in OverlayWindowController.handle(_:), show(), and fadeOutThenHide() reporting the state, whether the panel was created/ordered front, and RunLoop.current.currentMode. Then trigger an open from the menu on a real bundled build and read the log. Report what actually happens: is handle(.opening) reached at all? Is show() called? Does the panel order front and then get torn down early? Do NOT skip this — the fix depends on which it is.
2. Fix so the overlay is shown and completes its full hold-then-fade for a menu-triggered open, identically to the other two triggers. Candidate approaches, pick based on step 1's finding and justify:
   a. Dismiss the menu before firing the open (e.g. menu.cancelTracking() in menuOpenGate before dispatching), so the state fan-out happens outside tracking mode.
   b. Schedule the presentation work in .common run-loop modes explicitly, so timers/animations are not starved by NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode.
   c. Hop the openGate() dispatch to the next main-run-loop turn after tracking unwinds.
   Do NOT special-case the overlay per-trigger — the design is state-driven and must stay that way. The fix belongs in how the menu path yields the run loop, or in how the overlay schedules its work, NOT in an if-menu-then-show branch.
3. Preserve every existing guarantee: focus never stolen (orderFrontRegardless only, no makeKeyAndOrderFront/NSApp.activate), handle(_:) remains the sole presentation driver, the 9kk.5 reentrancy rules, the 9kk.7 settings-gate/stranding fix and Reduce Motion behavior, and the 9kk.9 hide() safety.
4. Remove ALL temporary logging before finishing; confirm with git diff.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A real bundled build, launched from /Applications, shows the overlay for a menu-triggered open, with the same hold-and-fade as a left-click. VERIFY THIS BY OBSERVATION, not by argument — a screenshot or a log line proving the panel was ordered front and stayed up for the hold. If the environment cannot drive a real menu click, SAY SO PLAINLY and hand it back for human confirmation rather than closing on reasoning.
- The other two triggers still work.
- swift build, swift test (126), and GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 (SELFTEST PASS) all still green.

title: Live door-camera view in the menu-bar app
description:
GOAL
When an open is commenced by ANY trigger (hotkey, menu item, status-item click), show the LIVE DOOR CAMERA in the overlay panel for one door session (~28-30s), then have the overlay DISAPPEAR. Also expose an explicit "View door" action so the camera can be opened WITHOUT opening the gate, to see who is there first.

CORRECTION — THIS EPIC'S EARLIER SCOPE DECISION WAS WRONG (2026-08-28)
An earlier version of this epic recorded, as settled and not to be re-litigated, that live video was unsuitable for the open-confirmation because its warmup would outlast the ~2s open, and that a canned animation was the right answer. THAT WAS A MISREADING OF THE USER'S REQUEST and is now retracted.
The user's original words were "a little video to pop up and run for as long as the normal video sequence". "The normal video sequence" meant THE DOOR CAMERA'S SESSION — the thing the ../comelit Python implementation already does — not a generic animation. A later message ("I did enable to keep the video going, but I don't think we need that for this app - just one 'scene' is enough") was likewise misread as endorsing the canned clip; "one scene" meant ONE ~30s DOOR SESSION, not one short animation. Confirmed directly by the user 2026-08-28: "I expect to see the gate, and I expect it to stay open for the roughly 30 seconds a scene plays."
The canned-animation overlay shipped under epic gateopener-9kk is therefore NOT the feature. It is a usable fallback for when the camera is unreachable, and — more importantly — it built the correct chassis: the HUD panel, the never-steal-focus guarantee, the state-driven presentation, the settings gate, Reduce Motion handling, and a deliberately swappable content seam. All of that is reused here unchanged; only the CONTENT changes.

WHAT THE ../comelit HISTORY ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES (surveyed in full 2026-08-28 — read this before designing)
PROVEN:
- The door streams H.264 320x240 to headless Chromium/libwebrtc. Frame-level proof, running in production in that repo.
- ICE/STUN/TURN candidate selection is NOT the blocker. Packet-level proof: a forced relay pair with DTLS connected bidirectionally on the exact 5-tuple still received zero application bytes.
- SDP TEXT SHAPE ALONE is not the blocker. Exhaustively tested against aiortc: ccm fir/nack/pli, exact profile-level-id values, extmaps, rtcp-rsize, ice-options, m-line ordering, recvonly and sendrecv-dummy — every variant gave DTLS connected, 0 RTP.
- The OFFICIAL Comelit iOS app uses STOCK GOOGLE LIBWEBRTC, not anything Apple-proprietary. Evidence: docs/ring-capture-2026-08-27/ in ../comelit, a WireGuard mitmproxy capture of a real doorbell ring on an iPhone. Its SDP carries extmap-allow-mixed, ice-options:trickle renomination, goog-remb, transport-cc, AV1, flexfec-03, red/rtx.
INFERRED ONLY — NOT PROVEN:
- "The door fingerprints the DTLS/SRTP stack." This is an inference by ELIMINATION (aiortc failed under every tested variant; Chromium worked). The discriminator was NEVER isolated: nobody compared DTLS ClientHello bytes, cipher suite ordering, SRTP protection profiles, extension ordering, or certificate/fingerprint algorithms. The memory comelit-video-solved-2026-08-25-the-door says "fingerprinting confirmed", but what was confirmed is the OUTCOME, not the MECHANISM. Treat it as a residual hypothesis.
TWO CONFOUNDERS NEVER RULED OUT — both are plain-protocol explanations needing no fingerprinting:
- (a) AUDIO LEG. ../comelit's own ring-capture README records that the door "negotiates down to PCMA/8000 even though the app offers Opus - offer PCMA or you get nothing" and "a two-section offer will not match this shape". The combination NEVER tested in aiortc: PCMA/8000 in a 3-section BUNDLE with a REAL, VERIFIABLY-TRANSMITTING sendrecv audio track (aiortc's dummy track's outbound RTP was never confirmed to actually reach the door). The door may simply require a live audio leg before it streams video.
- (b) OFFER CONTENT VALIDATION. The winning Chromium recipe REQUIRED --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=default because mDNS .local candidates made rtc/offer return HTTP 500; commit db32d22 in that repo calls this "the hidden blocker all along". That is the door being fussy about OFFER CONTENTS, not about crypto stacks.
NEVER TESTED: Safari/WebKit, iOS WebRTC.framework, GStreamer, Pion, werift, libwebrtc-direct. ../comelit's own open bead comelit-zj6.3 explicitly flags "CONFIRM Safari can actually establish the session before committing; a quick live spike is in scope" — and that spike was never run.

SETTLED BEHAVIOR (confirmed by the user 2026-08-28)
- ONE door session per activation, roughly 28-30s. NO renegotiation, NO reconnect, NO session continuation. Do NOT port ../comelit's stale-frame watchdog or renegotiation state machine — that entire subsystem exists only to survive the ~30s timeout and is explicitly out of scope.
- When the session ends, THE OVERLAY DISAPPEARS. It does not freeze on a final frame, does not show an error, does not attempt to reconnect.
- Stack choice was delegated to the implementer ("no preference, just figure it out").

CONSTRAINTS THE DESIGN MUST RESPECT
- Native resolution is 320x240 H.264. The existing panel is 240x180 (4:3) precisely to match.
- Signaling is ONE round trip, NO trickle ICE: PUT /servicerest/devicecom/endpoint/<ID>/rtc/offer with {"sessionId": uuid4, "offer": <full SDP, all candidates inline>} -> {"answer": <SDP>}. '#' in the endpoint id is replaced with %23 (NOT full percent-encoding). Wait for ICE gathering COMPLETE before sending.
- addTransceiver audio BEFORE video; the door's answer generation is m-line-order sensitive. Include a data channel, as ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html does.
- Pre-resolve the STUN hostname to an IP (stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com:3478). Passing the hostname caused iceCandidateError 701 in headless Chromium.
- Media flows P2P directly to the door on-LAN; Comelit TURN is fallback. SIGNALING always goes through the cloud, so every activation is an authenticated cloud call.
- The bearer token must NOT be handed to any web content, matching ../comelit's deliberate choice. Do the rtc/offer PUT from Swift.
- Door camera endpoint: friendlyName containing 'entry', else endpoint id suffix VIP#EN#SB100001.

REUSE FROM gateopener-9kk (already built and merged)
- OverlayWindowController: borderless non-activating NSPanel, orderFrontRegardless only, canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain false. THE FOCUS GUARANTEE IS THE ACCEPTANCE GATE and must survive: the user opens the gate by hotkey while typing in another app and must not lose a keystroke.
- setContent(_:) swappability seam plus the optional OverlayShowHideResponding protocol.
- handle(_:) as the sole state-driven presentation driver; the settings gate; Reduce Motion handling; the layer-BACKED content view (see gateopener-9kk.12 — a non-layer-backed content view makes the panel render nothing at all while still reporting isVisible=true).
- KNOWN TRAP, already filed as gateopener-12h.1: setContent(_:) on an ALREADY-VISIBLE panel does not fire overlayWillShow(), so swapped-in content sits un-started. This is exactly the ordering a live feed will use (show panel, then swap in the video view once frames arrive) and the symptom — a black tile — would look like a WebRTC failure rather than a lifecycle bug. Fix 12h.1 before or during this work.
- ignoresMouseEvents is already a constructor parameter, because the "View door" panel must be interactive/dismissable unlike the confirmation overlay.

SPIKE RESULT — gateopener-yjn PASSED 2026-08-28. THIS EPIC IS NOW BUILDABLE.
WKWebView (WebKit's OWN WebRTC stack, NOT libwebrtc) receives real RTP video from the door. Verified: rtc/offer HTTP 200, ICE connected, video.packetsReceived=5/framesDecoded=1, later cycle 9/5. The user also confirmed by eye, seeing the live camera view.
This OVERTURNS the inherited '../comelit' conclusion that the door only streams to genuine libwebrtc — that was an inference by elimination from aiortc's failure and does NOT generalize. Build on WKWebView; Google's WebRTC.framework xcframework is NOT needed.
WORKING RECIPE (plain, unmodified from ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html): 3 m-sections in BUNDLE order audio(0)/video(1)/application(2); audio recvonly with the browser's default codec list (PCMA present but NOT force-selected); video recvonly H264; datachannel via createDataChannel('data'); audio transceiver added BEFORE video; non-trickle ICE (wait for gathering complete, one-shot offer); rtc/offer PUT from Swift/URLSession with the bearer token never reaching page JS.
The PCMA / 3-section / transmitting-sendrecv-audio variant was NOT needed and never tried. Plain recvonly worked on the FIRST attempt.

TIMING — MEASURED, AND IT DECIDES THE PRODUCT SHAPE
Time-to-first-frame: 4431ms and 6003ms across two valid runs. A third reading of 1037ms is INVALID (that same log line reports framesDecoded=0 — a harness stale-flag artifact) and must not be cited as a fast path.
Verified against the raw logs: the dominant cost is THE CLOUD rtc/offer ROUND TRIP (1896ms and 2864ms across runs), not WebKit. First frame follows ~2.2s after the answer is applied. THIS IS NOT REDUCIBLE BY CHANGING WEBRTC STACKS — a native libwebrtc client pays the same cloud round trip. A cold token adds up to ~8s more (keychain + token refresh + endpoint discovery); a warm token removes nearly all of that.
CONSEQUENCE: ~4-6s is far too slow to front the near-instant gate-open confirmation (an open completes in ~2s). Live video belongs behind an EXPLICIT 'View door' action where a few seconds of connecting is expected and can be shown as connecting state. The canned-animation overlay from epic gateopener-9kk remains correct for the instant open-confirmation. Design a visible connecting state; do not leave a blank panel for 5 seconds.

TWO ASSUMPTIONS THE SPIKE DID *NOT* VERIFY — do not treat these as established
1. THE ~28-30s SESSION LIMIT WAS NEVER OBSERVED IN WKWEBVIEW. Every spike run was ended by the harness well under 30s (longest ~10-12s), so the door cutting the stream at ~28-30s is INHERITED FROM THE CHROMIUM FINDINGS, not re-proven for WebKit. This matters because the user's stated requirement is explicitly 'roughly 30 seconds'. AN EARLY TASK IN THIS EPIC MUST MEASURE THE REAL SESSION LENGTH under WKWebView by running one session to natural expiry and recording when RTP actually stops. Do not build the ~30s timing into the UI before measuring it.
2. STUN PRE-RESOLUTION NECESSITY IS UNPROVEN FOR WEBKIT. The harness pre-resolved stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com to IPs and injected stun:<ip>:3478 preemptively, mirroring the Chromium fix. Whether WKWebView would otherwise hit the mDNS-.local / rtc-offer-HTTP-500 problem was never tested. KEEP the pre-resolution — it is part of the proven-working recipe and is free insurance — but do not assert it is required for WebKit.
Also not captured: bytesReceived and frameWidth/frameHeight. If the UI needs real resolution rather than the assumed 320x240, measure it.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES CARRIED FROM THE SPIKE
- WKWebView needs an AppKit NSApplication run-loop context; it does not work from a bare CLI process. Fine here — this is a menu-bar app.
- GOTCHA: plain evaluateJavaScript(_:) fails with WKErrorDomain code 5 ('unsupported type') on ANY Promise-returning expression, confirmed on even a trivial Promise.resolve('world'). Use callAsyncJavaScript(_:contentWorld:) with an explicit 'return await ...;' body for anything async.
- The throwaway spike harness (NOT committed) is at scratchpad/webrtc-spike/ with main.swift, a webrtc_page.html copy, and run1-3.log. Read it before writing the production client.

NEXT ACTION
Run gateopener-yjn (the stack spike). It is the only thing standing between this epic and a real decomposition.

title: Picture-in-picture style HUD overlay confirming a gate-open attempt
description:
GOAL
Every way of commencing an open (global hotkey, menu item 'Open Gate', left-click on the menu-bar item) shows a small on-screen overlay that runs for as long as the open sequence lasts, so the user knows it worked without hunting for the menu-bar icon. Visible if you look, ignorable if you don't.

WHY
Today the only success feedback is the menu-bar icon swapping to a checkmark (GateIcon.image(for:)); NotificationPresenter deliberately only fires on .failed. When the open is triggered by the global hotkey the user is usually looking at another app entirely and may never see the menu-bar change at all.

SCOPE DECISION — CANNED ANIMATION, NOT LIVE DOOR CAMERA (decided 2026-08-27; do not re-litigate)
The Python reference implementation at ../comelit has WORKING live door-camera video. It is deliberately NOT used here. Reasons, all sourced from ../comelit's code and bd memories:
  - Warmup to first frame is ~2-5s in the reference (Chromium launch dominates). An open completes in ~2s. Live video would arrive AFTER the event it is meant to confirm, inverting the whole premise of the feature.
  - The door streams RTP for only ~28-30s per rtc/offer session, then goes silent; a new session requires a fresh AUTHENTICATED CLOUD round trip. There is no local re-offer path.
  - Native resolution is 320x240. Fine for a small tile, but it is a door monitor, not a confirmation.
  - Whether ANY Swift-side WebRTC stack even receives media is UNRESOLVED — see gateopener-9kk.9. Making the confirmation overlay depend on that would block a simple, valuable feature behind a research spike.
'Did it work?' and 'who is at the gate?' are two different questions. This epic answers the first. Live video is a separate, larger epic gated on the .9 spike.

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY (design constraint, not scope)
Build OverlayWindowController so its content view is swappable. A future live-door-view feature should be able to reuse the same HUD panel, positioning, focus behavior, and lifecycle, and only replace what is rendered inside it. Do not hard-code an AVPlayerLayer as the only possible content.

HIG POSITION (decided, do not re-litigate)
There is NO macOS HIG pattern for AVKit Picture-in-Picture used as transient feedback. macOS PiP (AVPictureInPictureController) is for user-chosen media playback and brings playback controls, a close button, a 'return to app' affordance, and user-repositionable persistence — all wrong for a ~3s confirmation.
The sanctioned macOS vocabulary for transient feedback is the HUD overlay panel — the primitive Apple uses for volume/brightness: a borderless, non-activating, floating NSPanel at a high window level that fades in, shows, and fades out without ever taking focus. That is what this epic builds. It is 'PiP-like' in look (small, rounded, corner-anchored, floats over full-screen apps) without being AVKit PiP.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN
- New app-layer type OverlayWindowController (Sources/GateOpener/) owning a borderless non-activating NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel style, isFloatingPanel = true, level = .statusBar, hidesOnDeactivate = false, collectionBehavior including .canJoinAllSpaces and .fullScreenAuxiliary, ignoresMouseEvents = true, canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain overridden false.
- Content is a short looping bundled video in an AVPlayerLayer inside a rounded, vibrancy-backed container.
- Driven purely by GateState transitions, exactly like GateIcon and NotificationPresenter. It observes state; it is NEVER in the call chain of openGate().
- Anchored top-trailing of the active screen, inset from the edges.
- Respects Reduce Motion and an AppSettings flag.
- Degrades silently on any failure (asset missing, no screen, unbundled process under swift run).

CONSTRAINTS
- GateOpenerCore must never import AppKit/AVFoundation/SwiftUI. All overlay code lives in Sources/GateOpener. The only Core change permitted is the AppSettings boolean flag (plain Foundation).
- Must not steal focus from the frontmost app under ANY circumstance. The user hits the hotkey while typing in another app and their typing must continue uninterrupted. This is the acceptance gate for the whole epic.
- Must not block, delay, or alter the open path.

title: Shortcut recorder field: click to activate, type the chord
description:
THE INTERACTION THE OPERATOR ASKED FOR: 'you click activate a text box widget of a certain kind, and then type the one you want.' This is the standard macOS shortcut-recorder control.

INPUT: ShortcutPreference/KeyboardShortcut in the core, GlobalHotkey.apply(_:) in the app layer, and the existing read-only GlobalHotkeySectionView in Sources/GateOpener/SettingsView.swift.

DO
1. Create a recorder view in Sources/GateOpener/ (e.g. ShortcutRecorderView.swift). It is a focusable, click-to-activate control that looks like a field, NOT a plain SwiftUI TextField — a TextField cannot capture arbitrary modifier chords.
   Implementation guidance: use an NSViewRepresentable wrapping a custom NSView that becomes first responder on click and overrides performKeyEquivalent(with:) / keyDown(with:) / flagsChanged(with:) to capture the chord. State your approach.
2. THREE VISUAL STATES, all clearly distinguishable:
   (a) IDLE showing the current chord (e.g. ⌘⌃⌥G)
   (b) RECORDING — visibly different (e.g. highlighted border and a 'Type a shortcut…' prompt) so the user knows keystrokes are being captured
   (c) NONE — a clear 'No shortcut' / 'Disabled' rendering. It must NOT look like an empty broken field.
3. While RECORDING, capture the chord and STOP recording. The captured keystroke must NOT leak through to the rest of the app or the system.
4. VALIDATION FEEDBACK IN THE UI: a chord with fewer than two modifiers is rejected with a short visible explanation (e.g. 'Use at least two modifiers — this opens your gate'), and recording continues or reverts cleanly rather than silently accepting or silently ignoring.
5. ESCAPE cancels recording and restores the previous value. This is essential — a user who activates the field by accident must be able to back out without changing anything.
6. A CLEAR / 'No shortcut' affordance (an x button in the field, and/or a Delete/Backspace keypress while recording) that sets the preference to .disabled. This is the operator's explicit requirement, so make it obvious rather than a hidden gesture.
7. A 'Reset to default' action restoring ⌘⌃⌥G.

description:
GOAL
A native macOS menu-bar app (MenuBarExtra) whose entire job is: when the doorbell rings while I am working, open the gate with one click, reliably, with no fuss.

WHY
The existing Python webapp in ../comelit works but requires a running server, a browser tab, and attention. A menu-bar app is always present, zero-latency to reach, and survives reboots. Scope at v1 is DELIBERATELY just 'open the gate' — no video, no intercom.

DECIDED (by the operator, do not re-litigate)
- Stack: Swift 6 + SwiftUI MenuBarExtra. Native app, no Python runtime. Auth/API logic is REIMPLEMENTED in Swift (URLSession + CryptoKit), not shelled out to the Python code.
- Credentials: username+password in the macOS Keychain. Tokens cached and refreshed.
- Endpoint: discovered on first login, auto-select the LOCK_GENERIC/PowerController actuator, cache the endpoint id, allow override in Settings.
- Trigger: LEFT-CLICK the menu-bar icon fires the gate IMMEDIATELY (no menu, no confirmation). Right-click (or a menu affordance) reaches Settings/About/Quit.
- Reliability: retry with backoff on transient failure; clear success/failure feedback via the icon itself.
- License: MIT. Public GitHub eventually, but NOT pushed at the start — local-only.

PROTOCOL FACTS ALREADY REVERSE-ENGINEERED (reuse, do not rediscover)
Reference implementation: /Users/ebowman/src/comelit/comelit/auth.py and client.py (validated live).
- BASE https://api.comelitgroup.com
- CLIENT_ID kgDV0WRlQcSF4jPsz887lOTPyVVtP7Oh
- REDIRECT_URI https://app.comelitgroup.com/oauth_redirect/comelit
- User-Agent: ktor-client
- Login is OAuth2 Authorization-Code + PKCE, 2 steps: POST /o-auth-2/auth (JSON) -> Location header with ?code=, then POST /o-auth-2/token (form, grant_type=authorization_code).
- PKCE verifier is a plain uuid4 STRING; challenge = base64url(sha256(verifier)) with padding stripped.

title: Self-replacing swap and Check for Updates
description:
INPUT: a verified DMG. OUTPUT: the self-replacing swap — the irreversible step.

READ THE REFERENCE CAREFULLY AND FOLLOW IT. A running .app cannot overwrite itself; the trick is a detached shell script that waits for the app to exit.

DO
1. Write a short /bin/sh script to NSTemporaryDirectory(), mode 0755.
2. Launch it DETACHED: `nohup ... >>/tmp/gateopener-update.log 2>&1 &` via /bin/sh -c, passing the DMG path, getpid(), the install dir, and the bundle name. EVERY interpolated path MUST go through a shQuote helper — these are paths from the filesystem and the bundle, and an unquoted space or quote here corrupts an rm -rf.
3. Then NSApp.terminate(nil).
4. The script: spin on `kill -0 $PID` until the parent is gone, then `hdiutil attach -nobrowse -noverify -plist`, parse the mount point out of the plist, `rm -rf` the old bundle, `cp -R` the new one into place, `hdiutil detach`, `open` the result.
5. Install dir and bundle name come from Bundle.main.bundleURL, so this works from /Applications or a build directory without special-casing. Do not hardcode /Applications.
6. Plist parsing: the reference shells out to python3. Keep that rather than grepping /Volumes — the reference explicitly calls the grep approach fragile. If python3 is unavailable, fail loudly rather than falling back to something unreliable.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY
Everything that can fail must fail BEFORE anything is destroyed:
- verify() throws -> the app stays intact.
- script write or launch fails -> throw launchFailed, the app stays intact.
- Once `rm -rf` runs, the ONLY recovery is /tmp/gateopener-update.log. So every step before it must fail loudly and visibly.
Do not reorder these. Do not "optimise" by unmounting or deleting earlier.

WHY cp -R IN PLACE, NOT A FRESH INSTALL — do not change this
Same path + same Developer ID identity means TCC grants, login-item registration, and THE KEYCHAIN ACL GRANT survive the upgrade. This project lost days to keychain re-prompts from an unstable signing identity (gateopener-sal); an updater that broke the grant every upgrade would reintroduce exactly that. Preserving it is a feature, not an accident.

DO
7. Wire a minimal user-facing path: a "Check for Updates…" menu item that fetches the manifest, compares, and offers to install. Keep the UI plain — an NSAlert is fine. DROP all the GPGuard Enterprise scaffolding: no custom UTI, no CFBundleDocumentTypes, no NSOpenPanel, no "it's been N days" nag. This repo is public so the app can just URLSession-GET the manifest and DMG.
8. Never take keyboard focus in a way that breaks the overlay guarantee. An update alert is a deliberate user-initiated interaction so it may activate — but do not disturb the overlay panel's orderFrontRegardless-only behaviour.

TESTING — be honest about what you cannot test
A real end-to-end self-replacement needs a genuinely notarized DMG and will terminate the app. Test what you can in isolation: shQuote correctness (spaces, quotes, backslashes, newlines), script generation given known inputs, and the ordering guarantee that nothing destructive is attempted when verify() throws. For the live swap, state plainly whether you performed it and against what artifact. DO NOT claim an end-to-end upgrade you did not observe.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.
- Do not weaken verify(); it gates this entire path.

- Nothing destructive runs when verification fails — proven by test.
- The script's generated text is asserted for known inputs.
- "Check for Updates..." exists and reports "up to date" correctly against a manifest whose version is not newer.
- swift build; swift test; SELFTEST PASS.

title: Port verify(): streaming sha256 plus notarization check
description:
INPUT: UpdateManifest/SemanticVersion. OUTPUT: UpdateInstaller.verify() — the security boundary.

THE REFERENCE IS EMPHATIC: "Keep verify() exactly as-is; it is the whole security story." Port it faithfully. Do not simplify, do not skip a check, do not make either check optional.

DO
1. Port UpdateInstaller.verify(dmgURL:manifest:) into Sources/GateOpener. It MUST throw unless BOTH hold:
   a. Streaming SHA-256 of the DMG matches manifest.dmgSHA256. Read in 1 MiB chunks — NEVER load the whole DMG into memory. A DMG is tens of MB and this runs in a menu-bar app.
   b. `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>` exits 0 — i.e. the DMG is Developer-ID signed AND notarized. Developer ID signing alone does not satisfy this.
2. Make it testable without a real signed artifact, as the reference does: both parts `nonisolated static`, and the notarization check INJECTED AS A CLOSURE so tests can substitute it. This is why the reference says the policy unit-tests without shelling out.
3. Tests must cover: matching digest + notarization ok -> success; digest MISMATCH -> throws (even when notarization passes); notarization FAILS -> throws (even when the digest matches); both fail -> throws. The two checks are independent gates and neither may be sufficient alone.
4. Each assertion must be non-vacuous — it must fail if the corresponding check is removed. State how you confirmed it.
5. Use a real temporary file of known content for the digest tests so the streaming path is genuinely exercised, including a file larger than one 1 MiB chunk so chunk-boundary handling is actually tested.

CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE c33.5 REVIEW — handle these here, they are NOT handled in the model
1. `dmgURL` is typed as `String` in UpdateManifest, deliberately, since Core is a pure model. URL VALIDATION IS THEREFORE THIS BEAD'S JOB. Before fetching or verifying anything, the URL must parse as a URL and MUST be https — reject http and any other scheme outright. A manifest is fetched over the network; an attacker who could serve a manifest naming an http:// DMG would otherwise get a plaintext downgrade on the very artifact that is about to replace the running app.
   Consider also pinning the host to the expected GitHub releases host derived from the repo, and say what you decided. Do not silently accept an arbitrary host just because the digest matches — the digest only proves the file matches what the MANIFEST said, and the manifest is the thing an attacker would control.
2. A version component >= 2^63 overflows Int and makes SemanticVersion return nil, which correctly fails closed but means the updater would SILENTLY stop offering updates forever. Not a defect, but if you surface any user-facing "up to date" message, make sure an unparseable-version case is distinguishable in logs from a genuine no-update, so this is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT implement the swap/install step here — that is the next bead, and it is the irreversible one. This bead is verification only.
- No networking here either.
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.

DONE-CRITERIA
- verify() throws on digest mismatch, on notarization failure, and on both.
- The digest path is streaming and provably handles a >1 MiB file.
- Tests pass and are non-vacuous by the stated method.
- swift build; swift test; SELFTEST PASS.

title: Port UpdateManifest and fail-closed SemanticVersion, with tests
description:
INPUT: the reference implementation's UpdateManifest.swift (manifest model + tolerant SemanticVersion). OUTPUT: the same, ported into GateOpenerCore with tests.

DO
1. Port UpdateManifest and SemanticVersion into Sources/GateOpenerCore (they are pure model/logic — no AppKit, no networking — so they belong in Core and are unit-testable there). GateOpenerCore must gain NO new import beyond Foundation.
2. UpdateManifest decodes {latestVersion, notes, dmgURL, dmgSHA256} and exposes `isNewer(than:)` comparing against the running app's CFBundleShortVersionString.

   - accepts 1-4 dot-separated integers
   - treats missing trailing components as 0, so 1.4 == 1.4.0
   - returns nil for ANYTHING else
   - an unparseable version on EITHER side means "no update available"
   Never prompt to upgrade to something you cannot order. This is a correctness requirement, not a nicety: a malformed manifest must never trigger an install.
4. Write thorough tests. This is pure logic with sharp edges, so cover: equal versions, strictly newer, strictly older, 1.4 vs 1.4.0 equality, 4-component versions, leading zeros, empty string, non-numeric components, negative numbers, absurdly long input, and nil-on-either-side. Assert that unparseable input yields "no update", never a crash and never an accidental upgrade.
5. NON-VACUOUSNESS: each assertion must fail if the corresponding rule is inverted. State how you confirmed it (see bd memory gateopener-vacuous-assertion-failure-mode for why this repo insists).

CONSTRAINTS
- No networking in this bead. Model and comparison logic only; fetching is a later bead.
- GateOpenerCore stays Foundation-only — no AppKit/SwiftUI/AVFoundation/Observation.
- Do NOT create a remote, run gh, or push.

DONE-CRITERIA

title: Release target: manifest generation and gh release publish
description:
INPUT: a notarized, stapled DMG. OUTPUT: a Makefile release target that generates the manifest and publishes both assets.

*** REQUIRES AN OPERATOR PREREQUISITE: a GitHub remote must exist. `git remote -v` is currently EMPTY. Agents MUST NOT run `gh repo create`, add a remote, or push. If no remote exists when this bead runs, STOP and tell the operator. ***

DO
1. Add a `release` target to the Makefile, following the reference Makefile.release-excerpt.
2. PRECONDITIONS FIRST — each turns a bad release into an early `exit 1`, and they are the cheap part of the value here:
   - VERSION non-empty (read from the BUILT bundle's Info.plist, per the version bead — never a shell literal)
   - working tree clean
   - tag v$(VERSION) does not already exist
   - the DMG exists and is notarized (spctl check passes)
   Fail with a clear message naming which precondition failed.
3. Derive host/owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin`, NOT hardcoded, so a fork or rename works without editing. Handle both ssh (git@github.com:OWNER/REPO.git) and https forms.
4. Generate the manifest with the digest computed from THE ARTIFACT JUST BUILT, so it can never describe a different binary:
     SHA=$$(shasum -a 256 "$(DMG_PATH)" | awk '{print $$1}')
   Manifest JSON: {latestVersion, notes, dmgURL, dmgSHA256}. `notes` is the release page URL.
5. THE MANIFEST FILENAME MUST BE STABLE ACROSS RELEASES (e.g. appcast.json) — that is what makes the /releases/latest/download/<name> redirect work. The DMG filename is versioned; the manifest name is NOT. Getting this backwards silently breaks update discovery, so assert it.
6. Publish both assets:
     gh release create "v$(VERSION)" --title "GateOpener v$(VERSION)" --generate-notes "$(DMG_PATH)" "$(MANIFEST_PATH)"
7. Document the whole flow in the README: build -> dmg -> notarize -> release, and what the operator must have set up (Developer ID, notary profile, gh auth).

CONSTRAINTS
- The target may RUN gh release create — that is its purpose — but ONLY when invoked deliberately by the operator. It must never run as a side effect of `make` or `make all`, and never from an unattended agent loop. Guard it so a bare `make` cannot publish.
- Do NOT create the remote or push branches; only `gh release create` against an existing remote.
- Do not weaken the notarization or signing steps.

DONE-CRITERIA
- `make release` dry-runs cleanly (or fails on a named precondition) with no remote configured — verify the failure message is helpful.
- The manifest's dmgSHA256 matches `shasum -a 256` of the DMG actually uploaded.
- The manifest filename is stable and the DMG filename is versioned.
- README documents the release flow.
- A bare `make` cannot publish anything.

title: Notarize and staple the DMG
description:
NO NEW KEY IS NEEDED — resolved 2026-08-28. The operator pointed at ../FlöDo, which already has working App Store Connect API credentials, and I verified them against Apple's notarization service:
    xcrun notarytool history --key ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_<ID>.p8 --key-id <ID> --issuer <ISSUER>
returned "Successfully received submission history" including a real prior submission (MCPMaestro-1.12.0.dmg, status Accepted, 2026-08-27). So this Apple account has already notarized DMGs with this exact key.
WHERE THE PIECES LIVE (operator's machine, NOT this repo, and they must never be copied into it):
  - Private keys: ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_7ZG885QRGL.p8 and AuthKey_JQR4S423V4.p8
  - Key ID and Issuer ID: exported as API_KEY_ID and API_ISSUER_ID in ../FlöDo/.env (gitignored there)
The only remaining operator step is a ONE-TIME convenience: storing a named keychain profile so scripts need no key paths.

OPERATOR STEP — run once, then tell the agent it is done:
    cd ../FlöDo && set -a && source .env && set +a && \
    xcrun notarytool store-credentials "GateOpenerNotary" \
      --key "$HOME/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_${API_KEY_ID}.p8" \
      --key-id "$API_KEY_ID" --issuer "$API_ISSUER_ID"
Verify with: xcrun notarytool history --keychain-profile "GateOpenerNotary"
(If the operator would rather not create a profile, the script must also accept --key/--key-id/--issuer via env vars. Support both; do not force the profile.)

CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE c33.2 REVIEW — check this early
The DMG's code-signing identifier is currently derived from the filename and TRUNCATES at the first dot: `codesign -dv GateOpener-0.1.0.dmg` reports `Identifier=GateOpener-0`. Harmless for a DMG in itself, but notarization is stricter than local signing. If notarytool rejects or warns about the identifier, pass an explicit stable one (e.g. `codesign --identifier ie.boboco.GateOpener.dmg ...`) in scripts/make-dmg.sh rather than leaving it filename-derived. Check this BEFORE burning a submission round trip — notarization is slow and each rejected attempt costs minutes.

AGENT WORK
INPUT: scripts/make-dmg.sh producing a signed DMG.
OUTPUT: scripts/notarize-dmg.sh that submits, waits, staples, and verifies.

WHY NOTARIZATION IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL
UpdateInstaller.verify() requires `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature` to exit 0. That passes ONLY for NOTARIZED artifacts — Developer ID signing alone FAILS it. Skipping notarization would gut half the security model and leave an updater that installs whatever the network hands it. It also stops Gatekeeper warning every downloader.

DO
1. Write scripts/notarize-dmg.sh matching the existing scripts' conventions (set -euo pipefail, REPO_ROOT derivation, header comment, clear failures). Read scripts/build-app.sh first and match its style.
2. Credential resolution, in this order, so it works for a contributor without the operator's setup:
   a. NOTARY_PROFILE env var (default "GateOpenerNotary") used via --keychain-profile
   b. else NOTARY_KEY / NOTARY_KEY_ID / NOTARY_ISSUER env vars used via --key/--key-id/--issuer
   c. else fail with the operator instructions above and exit non-zero — NOT a raw notarytool error.
3. Submit and wait: `xcrun notarytool submit "$DMG" ... --wait`.
4. On success staple and validate: `xcrun stapler staple "$DMG"` then `xcrun stapler validate "$DMG"`.
5. THE ACCEPTANCE CHECK — exactly what the updater runs, so it must pass here:
     spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature "$DMG"
   must exit 0. If not, the release is not shippable: fail loudly and print spctl's output.
6. On notarization FAILURE, fetch and print the log so the cause is visible:
     xcrun notarytool log <submission-id> ...
   A silent failure here is expensive to debug later.

CONSTRAINTS
- NEVER print, copy, commit, or transcribe key material, the Key ID, or the Issuer ID. Do not copy anything out of ../FlöDo/.env into this repo. Do not cat the .p8.
- Do NOT create a git remote, run gh, or push.
- Do not change signing behaviour from gateopener-sal.

DONE-CRITERIA
- ./scripts/notarize-dmg.sh takes a signed DMG through submit -> staple -> validate against the real service.
- `spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature <dmg>` exits 0. Paste the output.
- Running with no credentials configured prints the helpful instructions, not a raw error.
- No secret is committed; `git status` clean of key material; grep the diff for the key id and issuer to confirm neither leaked.

title: Build a signed, distributable DMG
description:
INPUT: a signed .app produced by scripts/build-app.sh, with the version now read from a single source.

OUTPUT: scripts/make-dmg.sh producing a distributable DMG of the signed app.
