3. Keep the DMG simple: a read-only compressed image (hdiutil create -srcfolder ... -format UDZO or equivalent) containing the .app and an /Applications symlink so drag-to-install works. No custom background art, no fancy window layout — those are cosmetic and can come later if the operator wants them.

title: Single authoritative app version, read back from the built bundle
description:
INPUT: scripts/build-app.sh, which currently hardcodes SHORT_VERSION="0.1.0" at ~:29 and writes it into Info.plist's CFBundleShortVersionString (~:96).

PROBLEM
The release process derives the git tag, the DMG filename, and the manifest's latestVersion from the app version. If the version lives in a shell variable while the bundle is built from that same variable, they agree today — but the reference design deliberately reads VERSION FROM Info.plist so the shipped bundle and the tag CANNOT disagree. Right now nothing enforces that, and a stale hardcoded value would silently publish a v1.2.0 tag containing a 0.1.0 bundle. The updater compares against Bundle.main.CFBundleShortVersionString, so a mismatch means users are told they are up to date when they are not.

DO
1. Establish ONE authoritative source for the version. Prefer a plain VERSION file at the repo root, or a single well-marked variable — pick one and justify it. build-app.sh reads it and writes it into Info.plist.
2. Provide a way for the release process to read the version back OUT of the BUILT bundle (e.g. `defaults read "$PWD/GateOpener.app/Contents/Info.plist" CFBundleShortVersionString` or PlistBuddy), so downstream steps use what was actually built rather than what was intended.
3. CFBundleVersion (the build number) should also be sane — it must increase monotonically for macOS to treat a replacement as newer. Decide how it is derived (git commit count is a common, reproducible choice) and document it.
4. Add a guard: if the version string does not parse as 1-4 dot-separated integers, build-app.sh FAILS with a clear message rather than producing an unversionable artifact. This mirrors the updater's fail-closed SemanticVersion.
5. Update any docs/comments that reference the old hardcoded value.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT change signing behaviour. build-app.sh signs with a stable Developer ID (gateopener-sal); that must keep working exactly as-is, including the CODESIGN_IDENTITY override and the ad-hoc fallback for contributors with no certificate.
- Do NOT create a git remote, run gh, or push.
- The app must still build and run identically.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The version appears in exactly one authoritative place; grep proves no second hardcoded copy.
- ./scripts/build-app.sh produces a bundle whose CFBundleShortVersionString matches that source, verified by reading it back out of the built .app.
- An invalid version string makes the build fail loudly.
- swift build; swift test; GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- The app still launches from /Applications and opens the gate.

title: Make a stale previous-session frame structurally impossible
description:
ROOT CAUSE IS NOW ESTABLISHED (gateopener-f8w.1, with screenshot + millisecond log evidence). READ bd memory `gateopener-f8w-root-cause-gate-open-path-overlaywindowcontro`.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — SIMPLER THAN THE EARLIER THEORY, WHICH WAS REFUTED
OverlayWindowController.handleOpening() (~:389-394) calls show() then startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled(), but NEVER calls setContent(_:). show() (~:192-208) merely re-fires overlayWillShow() on whatever content is ALREADY installed. startOpenVideoSessionIfEnabled() (~:413-444) builds a fresh DoorVideoFrameView but only installs it later, in handleOpenVideoState's `.streaming` branch (~:466-468).
  - FIRST open of a process: content is still the canned GateOpenVideoView, so the animation plays fully (2.2s) and holds its last frame. `.streaming` arrives ~6s later, well after it finished.
  - ANY REOPEN in the same run: content is the PREVIOUS session's DoorVideoFrameView, still holding its decoded image. show() re-fires overlayWillShow() on that STALE view (log-proven: `imageView.image=SET`), and it remains the panel's only content for a measured 2.5-6.3s until the new session reaches `.streaming`. That is symptom 1. And because nothing re-installs the canned view, the animation is never shown again either — that is symptom 2.
BOTH SYMPTOMS ARE THIS ONE OMISSION.

EXPLICITLY REFUTED — do not implement against it: the earlier theory that the canned animation is "torn out mid-play" by a premature swap on `.streaming`. Measured: the 2.2s clip finishes long before `.streaming` at ~6s. The swap timing is not the bug; the MISSING setContent on .opening is.

VIEW DOOR PATH IS NOT AFFECTED and needs no fix: DoorVideoOverlayController.start() calls setContent(connecting) synchronously before every session, so each reopen resets content. Two clean reopens verified, zero stale frames. Do NOT restructure that path. (Its swap-to-frame-view gap is ~150ms and imperceptible.)

THE FIX DIRECTION: make handleOpening() install content explicitly — the canned animation view — before/when starting a new video session, mirroring what DoorVideoOverlayController.start() already does. Then the reopen shows the animation again (symptom 2 fixed) and can never show the prior session's frame (symptom 1 fixed).

INPUT: the root cause established by the diagnosis bead (read its bd memory and report before starting).

OUTPUT: the overlay never shows a frame from a previous session, on EITHER entry point.

DO
1. Fix the actual cause identified by the diagnosis bead. Do not invent a different theory; if the diagnosis turns out to be wrong or incomplete, STOP AND REPORT rather than improvising a second fix.
2. THE BAR IS STRUCTURAL, NOT COSMETIC. A stale frame must be IMPOSSIBLE, not merely unlikely or short-lived. Do not fix this with a timing tweak, a sleep, or by shortening the window in which the old frame is visible. Concretely, the intended shape:
   - From the moment a session starts until a frame decoded BY THAT SESSION is displayed, the panel shows the connecting placeholder.
   - Any image belonging to a previous session is cleared at session start, rather than left in place to be overwritten later.
   - A frame is only displayed if it can be attributed to the CURRENT session.
   Whether that is achieved by clearing imageView.image, by always installing the placeholder first, by tagging frames with a session identity, or by ensuring no view/page outlives its session, is your call — justify it.
3. FIX BOTH ENTRY POINTS unless the diagnosis proved only one is affected:
   - "View Door" -> DoorVideoOverlayController (currentFrameView, ~:85/:161)
   - gate open -> OverlayWindowController (openVideoSession/openVideoFrameView, ~:412-422)
   If a single shared change covers both, prefer that over two parallel fixes.
4. Consider whether captureFrameJpeg should ALSO refuse to return a frame from a page whose session has ended. Resources/door-video.html:188-196 currently guards only on video.videoWidth/videoHeight being non-zero, and a finished <video> KEEPS its dimensions while frozen on its last frame — so that guard cannot distinguish live from stale. Hardening it is likely worthwhile defence in depth; say what you decided and why.

THE CANNED ANIMATION MUST BE VISIBLE ON THE OPEN PATH — a first-class requirement, not a side effect
The user: "I kind of liked the 'slowly opening curtains' effect, that distracts the user from the delay for live video to appear, and I didn't see that either."
Today OverlayWindowController.handleOpenVideoState(_:) (~:466) swaps to the live view on `.streaming`, which fires when the SESSION has framesDecoded > 0 — before DoorVideoFrameView has decoded its own first JPEG. So the animation is cut off mid-play and replaced by an image-less view showing a "Connecting..." label.
REQUIRED: swap to the live view only when a frame FROM THAT SESSION is decoded and ready to DISPLAY — not merely when the session reports `.streaming`. That single change plausibly fixes both symptoms: the curtains play through the whole connect delay, and there is never a window where the panel shows an image-less or stale view.
DONE-CRITERION FOR THIS: screenshot the panel DURING the connect window on a gate open and confirm the canned gate animation is visibly playing — not a "Connecting..." label, not a blank panel, not an old frame.

CONSTRAINTS — none of these may regress
- The overlay must NEVER take keyboard focus: orderFrontRegardless() only, never makeKeyAndOrderFront, never NSApp.activate. Verify by typing into another app while the panel is visible and report the observation.
- Keep the canvas-capture architecture; do NOT display the <video> element (it needs a key window the panel can never be).
- Keep the byte-comparison plateau detector: identical JPEG bytes must not count as a new frame, or session-end detection breaks.
- Keep streaming detection on framesDecoded > 0.
- Panel content view stays wantsLayer = true.
- Rapid repeated opens must still produce ONE panel and ONE session, not stacked ones.
- rtc/offer ONLY; never the power/open endpoint.
- Build with ./scripts/build-app.sh UNMODIFIED; add no codesign step.

VERIFY BY OBSERVATION, NOT ARGUMENT
Reproduce the ORIGINAL bug scenario and prove it is gone: run a full session to natural end, then start a second one, and screenshot the panel rect within the first 1-2 seconds. It must show the connecting placeholder or nothing — NOT the previous session's scene. Do this for BOTH entry points and report each separately, with the images described.
Then confirm the second session goes on to show live video normally and disappears at ~28-30s via the plateau detector.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Screenshot evidence that the second run shows no stale frame, for both entry points.
- Second run still streams live video and still ends via the plateau detector (not the hard timeout).
- Typing in another app is unaffected while the panel is visible.
- swift build; swift test (130 at filing, plus any tests you add); GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 -> SELFTEST PASS.
- git status --short shows only intended files; no leftover instrumentation.

title: Diagnose the stale-frame-on-reopen bug with reproduction evidence
description:
INPUT: the installed, working app on main (783a6b2). The user reports that opening the video overlay a SECOND time briefly shows the LAST frame of the PREVIOUS session.

OUTPUT: a definitive, evidence-backed root cause. NO FIX in this bead — diagnosis only, so the fix lands with the cause understood rather than guessed.

WHY DIAGNOSIS IS ITS OWN BEAD
Preliminary tracing RULED OUT the two most obvious explanations: DoorVideoOverlayController builds a fresh DoorVideoFrameView per session (~:85), OverlayWindowController builds a fresh one per open (~:422), and DoorVideoSession builds a NEW WKWebView per session (:174) loading the page fresh (:242). So this is NOT simply "the view was reused". Guessing at a fix without finding the real path risks papering over it.

DO
1. REPRODUCE IT FIRST, on the real app against real hardware, and CAPTURE IT. Trigger the overlay, let it stream, let it end (~28-30s). Then trigger it AGAIN and screenshot the panel rect in the first ~1-2 seconds of the second run, before the new session's first frame can arrive (~6s). Compare that image against a frame from the FIRST run. LOOK at both with the Read tool. You must be able to say "this pixel content is from the previous session" with evidence, not impression.
   Both entry points must be checked, and they use DIFFERENT code paths — report each separately:
     - "View Door" menu item -> DoorVideoOverlayController
     - opening the gate -> OverlayWindowController's openVideoSession/openVideoFrameView path
   Harnesses exist: GATEOPENER_VERIFY_VIEW_DOOR_MENU=1, and GATEOPENER_VERIFY_OPEN_VIDEO=1 with GATEOPENER_VERIFY_OPEN_VIDEO_TRIGGER=leftclick|menu|hotkey. The panel rect is printed by the harness; capture exactly that rect, never the full screen (the user is at the machine).
2. INSTRUMENT to find the path. Log, with timestamps: every setContent(_:) call and which view instance it installs; every DoorVideoFrameView init/deinit (use ObjectIdentifier so instances are distinguishable); every imageView.image assignment and whether the decoded bytes differ from the previous poll; every captureFrameJpeg result (nil vs data-URL length); and the panel's current content view identity at the moment the second session starts.
2b. DIAGNOSE THE SECOND SYMPTOM TOO — the user also reports the canned "slowly opening curtains" animation is NOT seen on the gate-open path, and they explicitly value it for covering the ~6s connect delay.
STRONG HYPOTHESIS, verify or refute: OverlayWindowController.handleOpenVideoState(_:) ~:466 calls setContent(openVideoFrameView) on `.streaming`, but `.streaming` fires when the SESSION reaches framesDecoded > 0 — before DoorVideoFrameView has completed its own first captureFrameJpeg poll and decode. The frame view has NO image yet and shows its own "Connecting..." label (DoorVideoFrameView.swift ~:251-252). So the canned animation is torn out mid-play and replaced by an image-less view.
If confirmed, this is likely the SAME root cause as the stale frame: content is swapped in before it has a current-session image to show. Report whether the two symptoms share one cause — that materially changes the fix.
RECORD: how long the canned animation actually plays before being replaced, and what is on screen in the gap between the swap and the first decoded frame.

3. ANSWER THESE SPECIFICALLY:
   - At the instant the second session starts, what view is installed in the panel, and does it still hold an NSImage from the first session?
   - Is the connecting placeholder shown at all on the second run, or is the old frame view left installed until new frames arrive?
   - Does captureFrameJpeg ever return a frame belonging to the previous session (e.g. a page/web view outliving its session)?
   - Are currentFrameView (DoorVideoOverlayController) or openVideoFrameView (OverlayWindowController) retained across sessions in a way that matters?
4. Record the root cause with `bd remember` in this repo so the fix bead and any future reader inherit it.
5. REMOVE all instrumentation before finishing; confirm with git diff.

CONSTRAINTS

- Do not regress or even touch: the never-steal-focus guarantee (orderFrontRegardless only), the canvas-capture architecture, the byte-comparison plateau detector, framesDecoded>0 streaming detection, wantsLayer on the content view.

Both symptoms trace to that one omission. Refuted the earlier 'animation torn out mid-play' theory: the 2.2s canned clip finishes long before .streaming arrives at ~6s, so on a FIRST open it plays fully; on a reopen it is never re-installed at all. View Door path is unaffected because DoorVideoOverlayController.start() calls setContent(connecting) synchronously every time. Recorded as bd memory gateopener-f8w-root-cause-gate-open-path-overlaywindowcontro. Diagnosis only, no production diff.

title: Sign the app with a stable Developer ID so keychain grants survive rebuilds
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-08-28 while working around an overnight keychain-prompt problem for the gateopener-yjn spike.

PROBLEM
scripts/build-app.sh:111 signs the app AD-HOC:
    codesign --force --deep --sign - "${APP_BUNDLE}"
An ad-hoc signature has NO stable code identity — the binary's identity is derived from its own hash, so it CHANGES ON EVERY REBUILD. macOS grants keychain access per code identity, so:
- Every reinstall invalidates the user's previous "Always Allow" grant for the Comelit credentials in the keychain (service "ie.boboco.GateOpener", account "credentials").
- The user is therefore re-prompted for keychain access after every single rebuild+install cycle, forever.
The install script already half-acknowledges this, printing "because the app is ad-hoc signed and just moved to a new path, macOS may prompt for Keychain access the first time it runs from here" — but the prompt is not actually a one-time path thing, it recurs on every rebuild.

THE FIX
The user HAS a real Developer ID certificate. `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` reports three identities; the relevant one is:
    "Developer ID Application: Eric Bowman (Y5SB82BPYL)"
VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (2026-08-28): signing with that identity produces a designated requirement keyed on the IDENTIFIER + TEAM, not on the binary hash. A probe binary was signed, its source COMPLETELY REWRITTEN, then rebuilt and re-signed — the designated requirement was byte-identical across both:
    designated => identifier <id> and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = Y5SB82BPYL
So ONE "Always Allow" would persist across all future rebuilds.

DO
1. Change scripts/build-app.sh:111 to sign with the Developer ID rather than ad-hoc.
2. DO NOT hardcode the identity as the only option — this repo is intended for public release (see gateopener-4ub.13), and a hardcoded personal signing identity would break the build for anyone else and leaks a team id into the repo. Make it configurable and DEGRADE GRACEFULLY:
   - Read an override from the environment, e.g. CODESIGN_IDENTITY.
   - If unset, try to auto-detect a Developer ID Application identity via `security find-identity -v -p codesigning`.
   - If none is found, FALL BACK TO AD-HOC (`--sign -`) exactly as today, and print a clear note explaining that keychain prompts will recur on every rebuild without a stable identity.
   A contributor with no Apple certificate must still be able to build and run the app.
3. Consider adding `-i <stable-identifier>` so the identifier stays fixed even if the bundle name ever changes.
4. Update the message printed by scripts/install.sh (~line 26 region prints the keychain caveat) so it matches the actual behavior in each case — stable-identity builds should NOT claim a prompt is expected on every rebuild.
5. Check whether `--deep` is still appropriate; it is deprecated by Apple for signing nested code and may warrant signing nested components explicitly. Do not change this speculatively — investigate and report, only change it if it is actually wrong for this bundle.

EDGE CASES / HAZARDS
- Do NOT enable hardened runtime or notarization as part of this bead. Those change Gatekeeper behavior and entitlements handling and deserve their own decision; this bead is only about a STABLE identity for keychain-grant stability.
- Signing with a Developer ID does NOT make the app notarized. First launch from /Applications may still show Gatekeeper UI depending on quarantine attributes. Do not claim otherwise in any user-facing message.
- Verify the existing keychain item is still readable after the identity change. NOTE: the user will likely get ONE more prompt after the first Developer-ID-signed build, because the identity genuinely changed from ad-hoc. Say so plainly in the report so it is not mistaken for a regression.

DONE-CRITERIA
- scripts/build-app.sh signs with a stable Developer ID identity when one is available, and still builds successfully with ad-hoc when none is.
- `codesign -d -r-` on two builds made from DIFFERENT source states produces the SAME designated requirement.
- The app still launches from /Applications and can read its keychain credentials.
- swift build, swift test (126 at time of filing), and GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 (SELFTEST PASS) all still green.
- No signing identity, team id, or certificate is committed to the repo.

title: SPIKE: does any Swift-side WebRTC stack receive RTP from the door?
description:
RESEARCH SPIKE with a single binary outcome. Time-boxed to ONE working session. It gates whether gateopener-12h (live door camera) is buildable at all.

THE QUESTION
Does a native macOS client receive actual RTP VIDEO PACKETS from the Comelit door station?

STACK CHOICE IS DELEGATED TO YOU. The user said "no preference, just figure it out." Test in this order, stopping as soon as one arm gets packets:
  ARM 1 — WKWebView. Cheap (~1 hour), and reuses ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html almost verbatim. WebKit's WebRTC is an INDEPENDENT implementation, NOT libwebrtc, so this is the genuinely unproven case — but if it works, the whole feature becomes trivial. ../comelit's own open bead comelit-zj6.3 flags this exact spike as needed and never run.
  ARM 2 — Google WebRTC.framework (libwebrtc) as an xcframework. Heavier, but it is THE SAME ENGINE that provably works in ../comelit's headless Chromium, and the same one the official Comelit iOS app uses. Low risk, higher integration cost.
If ARM 1 succeeds, ARM 2 is unnecessary. If ARM 1 fails, ARM 2 tells us whether the failure is WebKit-specific or universal — BOTH results are valuable, so run ARM 2 in that case.

READ FIRST — do not re-derive any of this by experiment
  cd ../comelit && bd memories --json    # NOTE: --json prints FULL bodies; bare `bd memories` truncates
Read in full: comelit-video-solved-2026-08-25-the-door, comelit-video-libwebrtc-fingerprint-theory-confirmed-on-2026, comelit-video-exhaustively-tested-aiortc-sdp-offer-fixes, comelit-video-black-screen-dies-at-30s-bug, comelit-video-protocol-captured-live-signaling-is-one, comelit-video-30s-timeout-is-real-and-cloud.
Also read ../comelit/comelit/webrtc_page.html (297 lines — the working recipe, and the page to reuse for ARM 1) and ../comelit/docs/ring-capture-2026-08-27/ (real iPhone SDP offer/answer from the OFFICIAL app).

WHAT IS PROVEN vs INFERRED — this shapes the spike
PROVEN: the door streams to Chromium/libwebrtc; ICE/STUN/TURN candidate type is NOT the blocker; SDP text shape alone is NOT the blocker; the official iOS app uses stock libwebrtc.
INFERRED ONLY: "the door fingerprints the DTLS/SRTP stack." Never isolated to any field — it is what remained after aiortc failed and Chromium worked. Do NOT treat it as fact.
TWO UNTESTED PLAIN-PROTOCOL EXPLANATIONS, either of which would make the fingerprint theory unnecessary:
  (a) THE AUDIO LEG. ../comelit's ring-capture README: the door "negotiates down to PCMA/8000 even though the app offers Opus - offer PCMA or you get nothing", and "a two-section offer will not match this shape". Never tested in aiortc: PCMA/8000 in a 3-section BUNDLE with a REAL, VERIFIABLY-TRANSMITTING sendrecv audio track. IF AN ARM FAILS, TRY THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING THE ARM IS DEAD — offer PCMA/8000, three m-sections, and a genuinely transmitting audio track.
  (b) OFFER CONTENT VALIDATION. Chromium needed --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=default or mDNS .local candidates made rtc/offer return HTTP 500. WKWebView also obfuscates host candidates via mDNS and exposes NO equivalent flag, so ARM 1 may hit this. Mitigation: a working STUN srflx candidate may satisfy the server without a real host candidate — testing that is part of the spike.

THE PROTOCOL (from the reference; do not improvise)
  PUT https://api.comelitgroup.com/servicerest/devicecom/endpoint/<ENDPOINT_ID>/rtc/offer
    headers: authorization: bearer <token>, content-type: application/json, user-agent: ktor-client
    body: {"sessionId": "<uuid4>", "offer": "<full SDP, all ICE candidates inline>"}
    -> 200 {"answer": "<SDP>"}
  '#' in ENDPOINT_ID is replaced with %23 (NOT full percent-encoding). Door camera endpoint id ends VIP#EN#SB100001 ("Entry"); find via friendlyName containing "entry" else that suffix.
Sequence constraints, all load-bearing:
  - addTransceiver audio recvonly BEFORE video recvonly. The door's answer generation is m-line-order sensitive.
  - Create a data channel, as the reference page does.
  - NO trickle ICE. Wait for ICE gathering COMPLETE, then send the full offer in one shot.
  - Use Comelit's STUN PRE-RESOLVED TO AN IP: stun:<ip>:3478 for stun.cloud.comelitgroup.com. The hostname caused iceCandidateError 701 in headless Chromium; pre-resolving is free insurance in any stack.
  - Do the rtc/offer PUT FROM SWIFT (URLSession), never from page JS — keep the bearer token out of web content, matching ../comelit's deliberate choice.

MEASURE EXACTLY TWO THINGS
  1. PRIMARY: RTP video packets received. Use getStats(): packetsReceived and framesDecoded. A BLACK VIEW WITH packetsReceived > 0 IS A PASS. A beautiful view with 0 packets is a FAIL and is precisely the aiortc outcome. Rendering, resolution, and frame rate are all OUT OF SCOPE.
  2. SECONDARY: TIME TO FIRST DECODED FRAME, wall-clock from starting the offer to framesDecoded first exceeding 0. Report in ms, ideally averaged over ~3 runs. ../comelit reports 2-5s but that is dominated by CHROMIUM PROCESS LAUNCH; native has no browser to start, and signaling alone is ~1s (ICE connected in 320ms). Sub-second is plausible but unproven. This decides whether the camera can front the open-confirmation or only an explicit "View door" action.

DO NOT BUILD
- No session continuation, no stale-frame watchdog, no renegotiation. One session, ~28-30s, then done. A session dying at ~30s is EXPECTED and is NOT a spike failure.
- No UI, no overlay integration, no production code in Sources/. Keep the harness OUT of the shipping target.

HAZARDS
- This makes AUTHENTICATED CALLS AGAINST REAL HARDWARE. rtc/offer starts a video session; it does NOT open anything. DO NOT call the power/open endpoint.
- Reuse this repo's existing auth path for credentials. Do NOT copy ../comelit/.env or its token cache into this repo.
- The door streams only ~28-30s per session; do not read a stream stopping then as failure.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A written verdict: PASS (name the stack, give packetsReceived/framesDecoded and time-to-first-frame) or FAIL (both arms tested, zero packets, with rtc/offer HTTP status and ICE state for each, AND confirmation that the PCMA/3-section/sendrecv-audio variant from (a) was tried).
- Record the finding with `bd remember` in THIS repo — whatever the result, it must not have to be rediscovered.
- No changes to Sources/ or the shipping app.
- Report the recommendation for gateopener-12h: which stack to build on, or that it is not viable natively.

title: Wire the overlay into AppDelegate for all three trigger paths
description:
INPUT
OverlayWindowController.handle(_:) from gateopener-9kk.5. Read Sources/GateOpener/GateOpenerApp.swift applicationDidFinishLaunching (around lines 52-100) to see exactly how notificationPresenter is constructed and how its handle is chained onto controller.onStateChange alongside StatusItemController.render(for:).

OUTPUT
The overlay fires for ALL THREE ways of commencing an open, with no per-trigger code.

STEPS
1. Construct an OverlayWindowController in applicationDidFinishLaunching and retain it in a stored property on AppDelegate, exactly parallel to 'private var notificationPresenter: NotificationPresenter!'. Without a strong reference the panel is deallocated and never appears.
2. Chain its handle(_:) onto controller.onStateChange next to the existing StatusItemController and NotificationPresenter handlers. Read the existing chaining code and extend it in the SAME style — do not replace the closure in a way that drops an existing observer. Verify after the edit that the icon still updates AND failure notifications still post.
3. Verify — do not assume — that all three trigger paths funnel through GateController.openGate() and therefore through the .opening transition:
   (a) the global hotkey (Sources/GateOpener/GlobalHotkey.swift and its handler),
   (b) the 'Open Gate' menu item (StatusItemController.menuOpenGate),
   (c) a left-click on the status item (StatusItemController.handleLeftClick).
   Trace each one and state in your report which line in each path reaches openGate(). If any path does NOT go through openGate() and thus would not emit .opening, STOP and report that as a blocking finding rather than special-casing the overlay for it — that would be a real bug worth its own bead.
4. Edge case: openGate() is documented as internally idempotent against a re-entrant call while one is already in flight. Confirm what state that emits (does a second call while .opening re-emit .opening, or nothing?) and confirm the overlay behaves sanely either way — mashing the hotkey must not stack panels or restart the animation jarringly.
5. Do not add any overlay call inside openGate() or inside any trigger handler. State-driven only.

CONSTRUCTOR SIGNATURE CHANGED IN 9kk.5 — READ THIS
OverlayWindowController's init is now `init(appSettings:ignoresMouseEvents:)`; appSettings is REQUIRED and there are currently NO call sites. You must pass the SAME AppSettings instance the rest of the app layer already holds — do NOT construct a fresh AppSettings() for the overlay. Constructing a second one risks reading a different UserDefaults suite than the Settings window writes to (this actually bites under GATEOPENER_MOCK=1, which uses a throwaway suite), which would make the Settings toggle appear broken. Find how AppDelegate already obtains AppSettings and reuse that instance.

DRIVE IT ONLY VIA handle(_:) — DO NOT ALSO CALL show()/hide() DIRECTLY
Finding from the 9kk.5 review: show() and hide() are non-private, but calling hide() externally while a resolve-fade is pending does NOT reset isResolveFadePending or cancel pendingResolveTask, so a later .idle would be silently ignored and the overlay could be left in an inconsistent state. The state machine assumes handle(_:) is the sole driver.
So: chain ONLY handle(_:) onto onStateChange. Do not call show()/hide() from AppDelegate or any trigger handler. If you find yourself wanting to, that is a signal something is wrong with the wiring — report it rather than working around it.

DONE CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds and 'swift test' still passes.
- Manual verification of the BUILT GateOpener.app for each of the three triggers, with the overlay appearing each time. Report each one.
- Menu-bar icon state changes and failure notifications both still work (regression check).
- No changes to GateOpenerCore.

title: Drive the overlay from GateState transitions
description:
INPUT
A working video overlay (gateopener-9kk.4). Read Sources/GateOpenerCore/GateController.swift (GateState, onStateChange, autoResetDelay), Sources/GateOpener/GateIcon.swift, Sources/GateOpener/NotificationPresenter.swift (its handle(_ state:) shape is the model to copy), and Sources/GateOpener/StatusItemController.swift's render(for:) plus its scheduleStillTryingCheck/escalateToStillTrying timer handling.

OUTPUT
The overlay appears and disappears purely as a function of GateState, matching the duration of the open sequence.

STEPS
1. Add 'func handle(_ state: GateState)' to OverlayWindowController, shaped exactly like NotificationPresenter.handle(_:) — a downstream observer of state changes, never in openGate()'s call chain.
2. State mapping:
   - .opening  -> show() and start playback.
   - .succeeded -> keep the overlay visible briefly to land the confirmation, then fade out. GateController auto-resets to .idle after autoResetDelay (currently .seconds(3)); the overlay must be GONE by then, so use a hold of about 1.2s then a ~0.25s fade.
   - .failed    -> fade out immediately (~0.25s). Failure is NotificationPresenter's job; the overlay must not linger and imply success.
   - .idle / .needsSetup -> hide immediately if shown; otherwise no-op.
3. Fade out by animating the panel's alphaValue to 0 via NSAnimationContext, then orderOut(nil). Reset alphaValue to 1 before the next show() — a panel left at alpha 0 that is then ordered front is an invisible overlay and is the obvious bug here.
4. Timer/reentrancy edge cases, all of which must be handled explicitly:
   - A second open commencing while the overlay is still fading out from the previous one: cancel the pending fade/hide, reset alpha to 1, restart playback from zero. Do not end up with a half-faded overlay.
   - .opening -> .succeeded -> .idle arriving in rapid succession (a fast open): the hold-then-fade must still complete and must not be cut short by the .idle that follows, NOR may .idle be ignored so long that the overlay outlives the sequence. Decide the rule, implement it, and state it in a comment. Suggested rule: .idle cancels nothing if a resolve-fade is already scheduled; it only forces a hide when no fade is pending.
   - A slow open (the 'still trying' case StatusItemController escalates on): the overlay keeps looping for the whole duration. No timeout, no max duration — it ends when the state resolves.
   - Store pending work as a cancellable Task or Timer held in a property, and cancel it before scheduling a new one. Follow whatever cancellation idiom StatusItemController already uses for its escalation timer.
5. Gate the whole thing on AppSettings.showOpenOverlay (gateopener-9kk.1): when false, handle(_:) is a total no-op and no panel is ever created. Read the setting at handle-time, not once at init, so toggling it in Settings takes effect immediately without a relaunch.

DONE CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds.
- A code path exists such that every one of the five GateState cases is handled, with no default-fallthrough that silently ignores a case.
- The reentrancy rules above are implemented and commented, not just described.
- No changes to GateOpenerCore.

title: Play the gate-open video inside the overlay panel
description:
INPUT
OverlayWindowController from gateopener-9kk.3 (placeholder content view) and Resources/gate-open.mp4 bundled by gateopener-9kk.2.

OUTPUT
The overlay panel's content is the bundled video, playing silently once per open and then holding its final frame for as long as the panel is shown.

STEPS
1. Replace the placeholder content view's contents with an AVPlayerLayer hosted in the layer-backed content view. Import AVFoundation in Sources/GateOpener only.
2. Load the asset with Bundle.main.url(forResource: "gate-open", withExtension: "mp4"). Edge case, and the important one: this returns nil when the process is NOT bundled — i.e. 'swift run' / '.build/debug/GateOpener' / the app's own self-test, exactly the case NotificationPresenter guards against with its bundleIdentifier check. When the URL is nil, show() must degrade to the placeholder/solid content or simply not show at all, log a notice, and NEVER crash or throw. Follow NotificationPresenter's silent-degrade precedent.
3. LOOPING — THE BEAD'S ORIGINAL ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG, READ THIS.
   This bead was written assuming a seamlessly loopable clip. The asset delivered by gateopener-9kk.2 is NOT seamlessly loopable: it opens and STAYS OPEN, so the first and last frames deliberately differ. Looping it would make the gate visibly snap shut and re-open, which reads as the gate cycling repeatedly rather than opening once.
   CORRECT BEHAVIOR: play it ONCE per open, then HOLD THE FINAL FRAME (gate open) for as long as the overlay remains visible. Do NOT use AVPlayerLooper. Do NOT seek back to .zero on end.
   Implement by letting the player reach the end and simply stay there — AVPlayer naturally pauses on the final frame at end of playback. Verify the last frame remains visible rather than the layer going black or blank; if AVPlayerLayer blanks at end-of-item on this macOS version, hold the frame explicitly (e.g. pause slightly before the end, or set the layer to display the final image). Report which behavior you actually observed.
   The overlay's total on-screen duration is driven by GateState in gateopener-9kk.5, NOT by the clip length. A slow open may outlast the ~2.2s clip; that is expected and is exactly why the final frame must hold.

4. Silence it unconditionally: player.isMuted = true AND player.volume = 0. Do not rely on the asset having no audio track.
5. Set videoGravity = .resizeAspect and make the AVPlayerLayer's frame track the content view's bounds on resize (layout via the view's layout method or an autoresizing/constraint setup — the panel is fixed-size today but must not break if that changes).
6. show() starts playback from .zero every time (seek to zero, then play) so a second open does not resume mid-animation. hide() pauses the player and, to avoid holding a decoder open indefinitely, releases or pauses cleanly. Report which you chose.
7. Keep the panel/focus behavior from gateopener-9kk.3 completely intact — no makeKeyAndOrderFront, no NSApp.activate. Re-verify this after the change.

DONE CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds.
- Running the BUILT GateOpener.app and triggering show() plays the video once and holds the final frame; the frontmost app keeps focus.
- Running the UNBUNDLED binary ('swift run GateOpener' or the self-test) does not crash and logs the degrade notice.
- No audio is audible.
- No changes to GateOpenerCore.

title: OverlayWindowController: a non-activating floating HUD panel
description:
INPUT
Sources/GateOpener/ (StatusItemController.swift is the closest existing model for an app-layer AppKit type). No video yet — this task builds the WINDOW only, with a placeholder solid-color content view.

OUTPUT
A new type Sources/GateOpener/OverlayWindowController.swift owning a borderless, non-activating floating panel that can be shown and hidden, and which provably never takes focus.

STEPS
1. Create '@MainActor final class OverlayWindowController'. It owns a lazily-created NSPanel. Do NOT create the panel in init — create it on first show(), so a process that never shows an overlay never touches window machinery (same lazy-degrade philosophy as NotificationPresenter's lazy UNUserNotificationCenter resolution; read that file's doc comment first and follow its style).
2. Panel configuration, all of which is load-bearing — put a comment on each explaining what breaks without it:
   - styleMask: [.borderless, .nonactivatingPanel]
   - isFloatingPanel = true
   - level = .statusBar
   - backgroundColor = .clear, isOpaque = false, hasShadow = true
   - hidesOnDeactivate = false
   - collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .stationary]
   - ignoresMouseEvents: default TRUE, but expose it as a CONSTRUCTOR PARAMETER or settable property rather than hard-coding it.
     For the confirmation overlay it must be true — the overlay is decoration and a click must always reach whatever is underneath.
     But gateopener-12h's 'View door' feature reuses this panel and needs it INTERACTIVE (dismissable by click). Making this configurable now costs one parameter; hard-coding it forces a rewrite later.
   - subclass NSPanel and override 'canBecomeKey'/'canBecomeMain' to return false. NSPanel with .nonactivatingPanel still becomes key on orderFront in some configurations; the override makes this unconditional.
3. Show it with orderFrontRegardless(), NEVER makeKeyAndOrderFront(_:) and NEVER NSApp.activate(...). This is the single most important requirement in this task: the user triggers an open by hotkey while typing in another app, and their keystrokes must keep going to that app.
4. CONTENT MUST BE SWAPPABLE — this is a deliberate forward-compatibility requirement from the epic. Do NOT hard-code the content view's type. Structure it so the panel owns a generic container NSView and the thing rendered inside is injected or replaceable (e.g. a 'setContent(_ view: NSView)' method, or a small protocol the content conforms to). RATIONALE: a future live door-camera feature (see gateopener-12h) should reuse this exact panel — its focus behavior, positioning, and lifecycle are the hard-won parts — and only replace what is drawn inside. For THIS task the content is a placeholder; the swappability is the deliverable.
5. Placeholder content: a rounded-corner NSView with a semi-transparent dark background (an NSVisualEffectView with .hudWindow material if straightforward, else a plain layer-backed view with cornerRadius). Sized per step 6.
6. Panel size: 240x180 points, a 4:3 aspect ratio. RATIONALE: the door camera's native resolution is 320x240 (4:3) per ../comelit — matching that aspect now means a future live feed drops in without reworking the panel geometry. Do not use a square.
7. Positioning: place the panel on the screen that currently contains the menu bar / mouse, anchored TOP-TRAILING, inset 16 points from the right edge and 16 points below the top of visibleFrame (so it sits under the menu bar, not over it). Compute from NSScreen.main ?? NSScreen.screens.first. Edge case: if there is NO screen at all (headless CI), show() must return without crashing and log a notice.
8. Public API: 'func show()', 'func hide()'. Both idempotent — calling show() twice does not create a second panel; calling hide() when nothing is shown is a no-op.
9. Add a doc comment on the type stating why this is a HUD panel and NOT AVKit Picture-in-Picture: macOS PiP is for user-chosen media and brings playback chrome, a close button, and user-repositionable persistence, all wrong for a ~3s confirmation. Keep it to a few lines.

DONE CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds.
- The content view is demonstrably swappable — a reviewer can point at the seam that would let a different view be rendered without touching panel/positioning/lifecycle code.
- Manual check: run the app, call show(), and confirm (a) a panel appears top-right, (b) the frontmost app stays focused, (c) clicking where the panel is lands on the app underneath.
- Report explicitly whether canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain were verified false at runtime.
- No changes to GateOpenerCore.

title: Produce and bundle the overlay video asset
description:

Resources/ (currently AppIcon.icns, AppIcon.svg), Package.swift, Makefile, scripts/.

OUTPUT
A short looping video bundled into GateOpener.app and loadable at runtime by name.

NOTE ON SCOPE: this is a CANNED animation, deliberately not live door-camera video — see the epic's scope decision and gateopener-9kk.9. Do not attempt to source real camera footage.

title: Add showOpenOverlay setting to AppSettings
description:
INPUT
Sources/GateOpenerCore/AppSettings.swift and Tests/GateOpenerCoreTests/AppSettingsTests.swift as they exist today.

OUTPUT
A persisted boolean preference controlling whether the open overlay is shown.

title: Operator check of the shortcut recorder
description:
OPERATOR-ASSISTED. The agent prepares; the OPERATOR performs and reports. Several behaviours here cannot be verified headlessly, and pressing the real chord opens a REAL GATE — the agent must never do that.

title: Persist and re-apply the recorded shortcut across launches
description:
Closes the loop: what the operator records in the recorder must survive a restart and be what actually registers.

INPUT: the model (task .1), the apply logic (task .2), and the recorder UI (task .3).

DO
1. Wire the recorder's output through to persistence: recording a chord saves .custom(chord); clearing saves .disabled; Reset-to-default saves .unset (NOT .custom(default) — keep 'following the default' distinguishable from 'happens to have chosen the default', so a future change of default carries through).
2. Route ALL writes through a single path (the controller/observable layer already used elsewhere) rather than writing to AppSettings directly from the view. A direct write from the view fires no change notification and bound UI would silently fail to update — this exact trap is documented in gateopener-4ub.7's notes.
3. On launch, read the persisted preference and apply it, so the operator's choice is live immediately.
4. After any change, the displayed state must reconcile to what is ACTUALLY registered — never show a chord as active when registration failed. If registration fails, show the failure and the still-working previous chord.

EDGE CASES
- Persisted .disabled must survive a restart as .disabled — the app must come up with NO hotkey registered, and this must be visibly presented as a deliberate setting, not a failure.
- If a persisted custom chord can no longer be registered at launch (another app took it), surface that in Settings rather than silently falling back to the default. Falling back silently would mean the operator presses their chosen chord at the gate and nothing happens, with no explanation.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Self-test asserts: a saved custom chord is registered on a fresh start; a saved .disabled state results in NO registration and no error message; .unset registers the default.
- Persistence verified through an injected throwaway UserDefaults suite in unit tests — the real ie.boboco.GateOpener domain must NOT be touched by tests (verify with 'timeout 15 defaults read ie.boboco.GateOpener' before and after: unchanged).
- Mutation-check the new assertions: break the re-apply-on-launch path and confirm the self-test FAILS with non-zero exit, then restore.
- swift test passes; zero warnings; SELFTEST PASS exit 0.
- SAFETY: mock mode only; never press or synthesize the real chord.
notes:
REVIEW 1: FAIL (2026-08-27). Production code is CORRECT; ONE done-criterion is unasserted.

THE GAP (criterion 6)
SettingsView.swift:188 correctly saves .unset for 'Reset to Default'. But NOTHING asserts it. The reviewer reverted that line to .custom(KeyboardShortcut.defaultChord) — the exact regression the bead names — and got SELFTEST PASS, exit 0, 120/120 tests green. The bead required 'verify in code, AND verify a test asserts it'. Code yes, test no.
This is the same vacuous-coverage failure mode bead .3 shipped in review 1, which is why the brief asked the reviewer to hunt for it.

WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: .unset means 'follow the default, whatever it becomes'; .custom(default) means 'I deliberately chose this chord'. If they collapse, a future change of default silently fails to reach anyone who pressed Reset. Nothing currently prevents that collapse.

WHAT PASSED (do not disturb)
- Single-write-path (criterion 5, the trap that bit this epic before): SettingsView -> recorderPreferenceBinding -> setPreference -> observable.setShortcutPreference persists AND applies in ONE call; the old apply-without-persist .onChange is deleted. Persistence and live effect cannot diverge.
- Two mutations DID fail correctly: neutering AppSettings.swift:93 (10 assertions flip, exit 1) and breaking the launch-apply at GateOpenerApp.swift:378 (6 flip, exit 1).
- Persisted .disabled survives a simulated relaunch as isDisabled true / isRegistered false / error nil.
- UI reconciles to live state after every mutation via seedFromLiveHotkey().
- Real ie.boboco.GateOpener domain untouched; core still Foundation-only; no secrets.

THE FIX — ONE ASSERTION, NOT A REWORK. Do not change production code.
1. In the persistence self-test block, route .unset through GateController.setShortcutPreference and assert the read-back is .unset AND that it is NOT EQUAL to .custom(KeyboardShortcut.defaultChord). The second half is what makes it non-vacuous — assert the DISTINCTION, not merely the value.
2. PROVE it: revert SettingsView.swift:188 to .custom(KeyboardShortcut.defaultChord), confirm SELFTEST FAIL with a NON-ZERO exit, restore, confirm PASS and byte-identical via shasum. Paste the actual FAIL output.
NOTE: the self-test trigger is GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1, not --self-test (which hangs).

title: Install script for /Applications, run by the operator
description:
WHY: GateOpener.app currently lives in the repo checkout. A real app belongs in /Applications, and SMAppService.register() (Launch at Login) is expected to fail outside it. OPERATOR DECISION: provide a script the OPERATOR runs — copying into /Applications may need admin rights, and the agent must not do that silently.

DO
1. Create scripts/install.sh (executable) that:
   a. Builds the app by calling the existing scripts/build-app.sh (do not duplicate its logic).
   b. Quits any running GateOpener instance first (osascript quit, or pkill on the bundle path), and WAITS for it to exit — copying over a running bundle is how you get a half-replaced app.
   c. Copies GateOpener.app to /Applications/GateOpener.app, replacing any existing copy.
   d. Relaunches it from /Applications.
   e. Prints clearly what it did and where the app now lives.
2. PERMISSIONS: /Applications is usually writable by an admin user without sudo. Try the plain copy FIRST; only if it fails, print the exact sudo command for the operator to run rather than invoking sudo yourself. Never call sudo unprompted from the script.
3. Be idempotent and safe to re-run. Replacing an existing install must not leave a partial bundle: copy to a temp path inside /Applications then atomically move into place, or remove-then-copy with a clear failure message if the remove fails.
4. Preserve the ad-hoc signature: verify with 'codesign --verify --deep --strict /Applications/GateOpener.app' after the copy and fail loudly if it does not validate (a broken signature would break keychain access and SMAppService).
5. Update the README 'Build and install' section to document scripts/install.sh as the normal path.

EDGE CASES
- The app may not be running (fresh machine) — quitting must tolerate that, not error.
- An existing /Applications/GateOpener.app may be running and holding files open — hence the quit-and-wait step.
- If the operator's keychain already holds credentials, the reinstalled app must still find them: the keychain item is keyed by service string, not bundle path, so it should survive. VERIFY this and state the result, because losing stored credentials on every reinstall would be a bad surprise.

DONE-CRITERIA
- scripts/install.sh runs end to end and /Applications/GateOpener.app exists and launches.
- 'codesign --verify --deep --strict /Applications/GateOpener.app' exits 0.
- Running the script a SECOND time succeeds (idempotent) and does not leave a partial bundle.
- The script never invokes sudo on its own; if it cannot write, it prints the exact command for the operator.
- The bundled app at its new location still passes GATEOPENER_MOCK=1 GATEOPENER_MOCK_SELFTEST=1 with SELFTEST PASS.
- DO NOT run a real (non-mock) gate open as part of verification.

NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: you may CREATE and TEST the script, but the actual /Applications install is the operator's to run if it requires admin rights. If the plain copy works without elevation, running it is fine — report exactly what you did.

title: Global hotkey to open the gate from anywhere
description:
WHY: the status item is currently unreachable — measured live at x = -10329 on a 1352-point screen, because macOS parks overflow status items off-screen when the menu bar is full (the operator's is). The app is healthy but its one-click affordance cannot be clicked. A global hotkey makes the gate reachable regardless of menu bar space. OPERATOR DECISION: add this; it complements click-to-open rather than replacing it.

DO
1. Register a system-wide hotkey that calls the SAME code path as a left-click: 'Task { await controller.openGate() }'. Do NOT duplicate the open logic — reuse GateController.openGate(), which is already idempotent against double-fires.
2. Choose the API deliberately and justify it: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey is the long-standing approach and needs no special permission; NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents requires Accessibility permission (a worse first-run experience). Prefer an approach that does NOT require Accessibility permission, and say why in your report.
3. Pick a safe default that is unlikely to collide with system or app shortcuts. Suggest something like Cmd-Ctrl-Alt-G, but VERIFY it is not already taken by a macOS default and state what you checked.
4. Make the hotkey CONFIGURABLE or at least clearly documented. A hardcoded shortcut that collides with something the operator uses is a real problem. If a full recorder UI is too large for this task, expose the current shortcut read-only in Settings and file a follow-up for making it editable — do not silently hardcode with no visible indication.
5. Handle registration failure gracefully: if the hotkey is already claimed by another app, do NOT crash and do NOT fail silently. Surface it in Settings (e.g. 'Shortcut unavailable — another app is using it').
6. SAFETY: the hotkey fires a REAL gate open. It must not be triggerable by an ordinary keystroke — require a multi-modifier combination. Consider and state whether accidental firing is plausible.

EDGE CASES
- The hotkey must work when the app is not frontmost (that is the whole point).
- It must not fire while the Settings window has focus and the user is typing a password (verify: a multi-modifier chord will not collide with normal typing, but confirm the behaviour).
- If state is .needsSetup, the hotkey must NOT attempt a doomed open — mirror the left-click behaviour (open Settings instead).

DONE-CRITERIA
- swift build / --build-tests: ZERO warnings; swift test: existing tests still pass.
- MACHINE-CHECKABLE under GATEOPENER_MOCK=1: extend the self-test to programmatically invoke the hotkey handler (not a synthesized system keystroke) and assert it results in EXACTLY ONE openGate() call on the mock, and ZERO when state is .needsSetup. Report actual output.
- Registration failure path exercised (e.g. by attempting to register an already-taken combination) and shown to surface a message rather than crash.
- NEVER test by firing a real open. Mock mode only.

title: End-to-end live verification against the real gate (operator-assisted)
description:
INPUT: the packaged app from .11. THIS TASK REQUIRES THE HUMAN OPERATOR — it opens a real physical gate. Do not run it unattended, and do not fire repeated live opens 'to be sure'.

DO
1. Confirm with the operator that they are ready and that firing the gate now is acceptable.
2. Fresh-install path: with no prior keychain entry, launch the app, confirm it lands in .needsSetup and auto-opens Settings.

(h) SMAppService.register() succeeding from a real /Applications install. IMPORTANT: specifically test a DENIAL too — deny it in System Settings > General > Login Items and confirm the message says Launch at Login was denied and points at Login Items, NOT 'Move GateOpener to /Applications first'. That misattribution was a real bug (wrong SMError constant) fixed during review; this is the check that confirms the fix in the field.

They launched the app, signed in with real credentials (authentication succeeded), discovery selected the gate, and clicking the Test button OPENED THE REAL PHYSICAL GATE. That validates the whole stack end to end: OAuth2+PKCE login, keychain storage, endpoint discovery with the Generic Actuator correctly excluded, percent-encoded endpoint id, and the open command. title: Settings window: sign in, change password, pick the gate, sign out
description:
INPUT: GateController (.7) and the app shell (.8).

DO
1. Add a SwiftUI Settings scene / window (opened from the right-click menu and auto-opened when .needsSetup).
2. Sign-in form: username (email) and password (SecureField), plus a Sign In button. On submit call controller.performFirstTimeSetup. Show an inline progress indicator and an inline error — never a modal alert for a wrong password.
3. When already signed in show: the signed-in username, the currently selected gate's friendly name, a 'Change password…' affordance that re-saves credentials to the keychain and re-logs in, and a 'Sign Out' button that calls controller.signOut() with a confirmation.
4. Gate picker: a Refresh button re-runs discovery and shows candidate gates in a Picker bound to AppSettings.selectedEndpointId. Display friendlyName plus the display category. The excluded Generic Actuator must NOT appear in this list.
5. An aptId field, shown as an advanced/fallback control (see the ambiguity flagged in .7) — prefilled from discovery when it can be derived.
6. A 'Test' button that fires an open command and reports the result inline, so the user can verify setup without walking to the gate. Label it clearly — it really does open the gate.
7. The password field must never be echoed, logged, or persisted anywhere except the keychain.

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds; the window opens from the menu and from the auto-open-on-needsSetup path.
- Signing in with deliberately wrong credentials shows 'Wrong username or password' inline and leaves state at .needsSetup.
- After a successful sign-in the window shows the resolved gate name, and the menu-bar icon leaves the .needsSetup appearance.
- Sign Out clears the keychain entry (verify: relaunching the app returns to .needsSetup).

EDGE CASES
- Sign In must be disabled while a sign-in is in flight, and while either field is empty.
- Discovery failures during Refresh show inline, and must not clear an already-working selection.
notes:
REVIEW: PASS (2026-08-27). Verified: no aptId control anywhere (cancelled part confirmed absent); SecureField + inline progress/error, never a modal for a wrong password; Sign In disabled while in flight and on empty fields; exact 'Wrong username or password' string; Sign Out behind a destructive confirmationDialog; Refresh failure sets refreshError WITHOUT touching candidates (selection preserved); Test button labelled 'Test — this will actually open the gate'; ZERO print/NSLog/os_log in SettingsView; password copied to a local, passed only to the controller, cleared in a defer on BOTH success and failure paths; all mutations route through observable.controller.
JUDGED NON-BLOCKING: (1) the direct-read compromise — SettingsView reads KeychainCredentialStore().loadCredentials()?.username and AppSettings() directly for DISPLAY ONLY (:216, :220, :381); all three sites are genuinely read-only, and under mock mode the shown gate name may be stale/blank, but it CANNOT cause a wrong gate to open because openGate() uses the controller's own settings. Follow-up filed to add a read accessor on GateController. (2) GateControllerObservable.appShared static — a mild global-state smell, guarded by assertionFailure rather than a force-unwrap, existing only because showShared()'s signature is pinned by off-limits call sites in StatusItemController.swift. Honest fix is DI when that file is editable.

title: MenuBarExtra app shell: left-click opens the gate immediately, right-click shows the menu
description:
INPUT: GateController from .7.

THE CORE UX DECISION (from the operator, do not change): a LEFT-CLICK on the menu-bar icon fires the gate IMMEDIATELY — no menu, no confirmation dialog, no second click. The whole point is that the bell rings and one click opens the gate.

DO
1. Sources/GateOpener/GateOpenerApp.swift: an @main App with a MenuBarExtra scene, LSUIElement/.accessory activation policy so NO Dock icon and NO app window appear.
2. SwiftUI's MenuBarExtra does not cleanly give left-click-action + right-click-menu. Use an NSStatusItem-based approach (an AppKit NSApplicationDelegate creating NSStatusItem, with the button's sendAction(on:) covering leftMouseUp and rightMouseUp) and drive it from the SwiftUI app lifecycle. Distinguish the click via NSApp.currentEvent.type.
   - LEFT click -> Task { await controller.openGate() }
   - RIGHT click (or Control-click) -> pop up an NSMenu with: Open Gate, Settings…, About, Quit (with Cmd-Q).
3. Icon rendering reflects GateState, template-rendered so it adapts to light/dark menu bars:
   - .idle -> a gate/lock SF Symbol
   - .opening -> a visibly distinct in-progress appearance (SF Symbol swap or subtle animation — do NOT use a spinner that steals focus)
   - .succeeded -> a checkmark variant
   - .failed -> an exclamation variant
   - .needsSetup -> a badged/greyed variant, and a left-click in this state opens Settings rather than firing a doomed command.
4. Tooltip shows the current state's message.
5. If state is .needsSetup on launch, open the Settings window once, automatically.

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift build' succeeds and the app runs: the icon appears in the menu bar, no Dock icon, no stray window.
- A left-click with a MOCK controller (a build/run flag or a debug menu is acceptable) demonstrably calls openGate() exactly once; a right-click shows the menu and does NOT fire openGate.
- Icon visibly changes across all five states.
- Quit actually terminates the process.

EDGE CASES
- Do not let a left-click while .opening enqueue a second open — the controller already guards this, but the UI must not spin up parallel Tasks either.
- The app must not crash if the status item cannot be created (menu bar full) — log and exit gracefully with a user-visible alert.
notes:
LATENCY DATA (measured live 2026-08-27, read-only): the Comelit cloud's NORMAL response time is ~1.6-1.9s per call (median 1702ms). So a successful gate open typically takes roughly 2s end-to-end, NOT the 15s worst case. The 15s path only happens when the cloud is actually failing (3 attempts x 3s timeout + ~6s bounded backoff).
UX IMPLICATION FOR THE ICON: .opening will normally last ~2s — long enough that the icon MUST visibly change immediately on click (the user needs instant feedback that their click registered), but short enough that an elaborate progress UI is unnecessary. Do NOT show a countdown or attempt counter. A simple, clearly-distinct .opening appearance is right.
DO NOT tighten GateClient's requestTimeout to shave the worst case — 3s is only ~1.1s above normal latency, and tightening it would spuriously time out healthy requests and cause unnecessary retries against a physical gate.

title: GateController: the single facade the UI drives, with an observable state machine
description:
INPUT: TokenManager (.4), GateClient (.5), AppSettings (.6).

WHY THIS EXISTS: the UI must be dumb. All orchestration, error mapping, and state lives here so it is testable without a GUI.

DO
1. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/GateController.swift — a @MainActor @Observable (or ObservableObject) class.
2. 'enum GateState: Equatable': .needsSetup, .idle, .opening, .succeeded(at: Date), .failed(message: String). Every case must carry everything the icon needs to render.
3. 'func openGate() async' — the ONE method the menu-bar click calls. It must:
   a. Be idempotent against double-clicks: if state is already .opening, return immediately without firing a second command. This matters — a nervous double-click must not send two opens.
   b. Set .opening, resolve the token, PUT the open command via GateClient (which handles retry), then set .succeeded or .failed.
   c. Auto-return to .idle after ~3 seconds from .succeeded/.failed so the icon settles back.
4. Map errors to SHORT human messages suitable for a menu-bar tooltip / notification: .invalidCredentials -> 'Wrong username or password'; .notConfigured -> routes to .needsSetup instead of .failed; network/server exhaustion -> 'Could not reach the gate'; noEndpointsFound -> 'No gate found'. No raw error dumps in the UI.
5. 'func performFirstTimeSetup(username:password:) async throws' — saves credentials, logs in, discovers, auto-selects the top candidate gate (LOCK_GENERIC first), persists aptId + endpoint to AppSettings.
6. If AppSettings has no aptId, obtain it during setup. Look at how /Users/ebowman/src/comelit derives it; if the API does not expose an apartment list, this is an AMBIGUITY — implement a Settings text field for the aptId as the fallback and note it in the code, do not silently hardcode the operator's aptId.
7. 'func signOut()' clears keychain credentials, tokens, and settings, returning to .needsSetup.

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift test' passes with tests using mock client/store: a successful open transitions idle->opening->succeeded; a failing open ends in .failed with a short message; calling openGate() twice concurrently results in exactly ONE underlying open call; .notConfigured routes to .needsSetup not .failed; signOut() returns to .needsSetup and clears the store (assert the mock store was cleared).
- Time-based auto-reset to .idle is tested with an injected clock/delay, not a real 3-second sleep.

EDGE CASES
- Clock skew / system sleep between succeeded and reset must not wedge the state — reset is best-effort.
- A failure must never leave state stuck in .opening; use defer or equivalent.
notes:
OBSERVABILITY CONSTRAINT (from the bead .6 review — read before implementing).

AppSettings (Sources/GateOpenerCore/AppSettings.swift) is a PLAIN, NON-OBSERVABLE final class. It imports Foundation only — deliberately no @Observable, no ObservableObject, no Combine — because GateOpenerCore must stay free of SwiftUI/AppKit/Observation so it remains headlessly testable. That constraint comes from bead .1 and is load-bearing.

THEREFORE, when implementing GateController:
- DO NOT 'fix' this by adding @Observable/@Published/ObservableObject to AppSettings. That would silently break bead .1's constraint and is explicitly forbidden.
- GateController itself is app-side and MAY be @Observable/@MainActor.
- GateController must HOLD an AppSettings instance and RE-PUBLISH what the UI needs (e.g. expose selectedEndpointName / isConfigured as its own observable properties, refreshed after any mutation).
- ROUTE ALL WRITES THROUGH GateController. A direct write to AppSettings fires NO change notification, so any UI bound to it would silently fail to update. This is the specific trap to avoid.

title: GateClient: endpoint discovery, gate selection, and the open command with retry+backoff
description:
INPUT: TokenManager from .4. Reference implementation: /Users/ebowman/src/comelit/comelit/client.py.

DO
1. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/GateClient.swift.
2. 'func discover(aptId: String) async throws -> [Endpoint]' — GET /servicerest/devicecom/endpoints/discovery?aptId=... with bearer auth and User-Agent ktor-client. 'struct Endpoint: Codable, Identifiable' with endpointId, friendlyName, capabilities [String], displayCategories [String].
3. 'func candidateGates(from: [Endpoint]) -> [Endpoint]' — keep endpoints whose capabilities contain 'PowerController'; ORDER them so a displayCategories containing 'LOCK_GENERIC' sorts first. CRITICAL: EXCLUDE any endpoint whose id ends with 'VIP#OD#SBIO0255.0' — that is the 'Generic Actuator', which returns 202 but does nothing physical, and must never be offered as the gate. Put that exclusion behind a named constant with a comment explaining why.
4. 'func open(endpointId: String) async throws' — PUT /servicerest/devicecom/endpoint/<percent-encoded endpointId>/power, body {"value":true}, JSON content-type, bearer auth. Percent-encode '#' and all other reserved characters (the id contains '#'). Success is HTTP 202; also accept 200 defensively.
5. RETRY, and treat it as required not optional: the Comelit cloud transiently 500s on this exact call and the official app sends it twice. Retry on HTTP 5xx, on 429, and on transport errors. Do NOT retry 4xx other than 429. On HTTP 401, call tokenManager.invalidate() and retry ONCE with a fresh token.
6. Backoff: 3 attempts by default, exponential from ~400ms with jitter, total wall-clock bounded to ~6 seconds. Bounded because a human is standing at the gate — failing fast and clearly beats hanging.
7. Make attempt count / delays injectable so tests run instantly without real sleeping.
8. NEVER send {"value":false} — the API 500s on it. Do not implement a close/toggle at all.

- Tests complete in well under a second (no real backoff sleeps).

EDGE CASES
- discovery may return an empty array (account not provisioned) -> throw a distinct .noEndpointsFound.
- If candidateGates is empty after filtering, that is a distinct error the UI must surface as 'no gate found', not a generic failure.
notes:
REVIEW 1: FAIL (2026-08-27). Five defects, each empirically proven by the reviewer with probes, not inferred:
1. BLOCKING GateClient.swift:359-360 — 'catch let error as ComelitError { throw error }' intercepts wrapped transport errors BEFORE the transport-retry branch at :361-367, making that branch dead code. Probe: URLError(.networkConnectionLost) => 1 attempt, expected 3.

LOCK_GENERIC is used only for RANKING, never exclusion. The doc comment at :227-228 falsely claims both discriminators are enforced. Probe: an endpoint with displayCategories ['VIP_ACTUATOR'] and a non-matching id SURVIVES candidateGates.

5. NON-BLOCKING — no timeoutIntervalForRequest; a hanging server can block ~180s (3 x 60s default) despite the '~6s bounded' intent. maxTotalDelay bounds sleep, not request time.
PASSED: percent-encoding (verified byte-identical to the Python reference by the orchestrator), never sends value:false, aptId omitted when nil, distinct error cases, sanitized fixture, no secret logging, offline tests, sound jitter, .invalidCredentials never retried.

title: TokenManager: cached tokens with automatic refresh and re-login
description:
INPUT: ComelitAPI (login/refresh) from .2 and CredentialStoring from .3.

DO
1. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/TokenManager.swift: an actor (Swift concurrency) owning token lifecycle.
2. 'func accessToken() async throws -> String' resolves in this order:
   a. A cached in-memory token that is not near expiry -> return it.
   b. A token loaded from the credential store that is not near expiry -> cache and return.
   c. Otherwise attempt refresh() with the stored refresh token; on success persist + return.
   d. If refresh fails, fall back to a full login() using stored username/password; persist + return.
   e. If there are no stored credentials at all, throw .notConfigured so the UI can prompt for setup.
3. Treat a token as expired if it expires within a 5-minute skew window. Never hand out a token about to die mid-request.
4. Because it is an actor, CONCURRENT callers must not trigger multiple simultaneous logins — the second caller awaits the first's result. Implement and test this coalescing explicitly.
5. 'func invalidate()' drops the cached token (used when the server rejects a token mid-flight, so the next call re-authenticates).
6. TokenManager takes its API client and credential store as injected protocol dependencies so tests need no network.

DONE-CRITERIA
- 'swift test' passes with tests covering: fresh-token hit, expired-token triggers refresh, failed-refresh falls back to full login, missing credentials throws .notConfigured, and TWO concurrent accessToken() calls with an empty cache produce exactly ONE login call (assert with a counter in the mock).
- No token value appears in any log statement.

EDGE CASES
- Refresh tokens can be rejected as expired/revoked -> must silently fall through to full login, not surface an error.
- If full login fails with .invalidCredentials, propagate that distinctly — the UI needs to tell the user their password is wrong rather than retrying forever.

title: Keychain-backed credential store
description:
INPUT: the scaffolded GateOpenerCore target.

DO
1. Add Sources/GateOpenerCore/CredentialStore.swift defining 'protocol CredentialStoring' with: saveCredentials(username:password:), loadCredentials() -> (username,password)?, deleteCredentials(), saveTokens(TokenSet), loadTokens() -> TokenSet?, deleteTokens(). All throwing where appropriate.
2. Implement 'KeychainCredentialStore: CredentialStoring' using the Security framework (SecItemAdd/SecItemCopyMatching/SecItemUpdate/SecItemDelete) with kSecClassGenericPassword, a service string like 'ie.boboco.GateOpener', and distinct accounts for the password vs the token blob.
3. Tokens are stored as JSON-encoded TokenSet in the keychain too — NOT in UserDefaults and NOT in a plaintext file. Rationale: the refresh token is as sensitive as the password.
4. Use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock (or better) so the app can refresh tokens after a reboot without the user being logged in interactively first.
5. Implement an in-memory 'MockCredentialStore: CredentialStoring' in the TEST target for use by later tasks.
